items.title: Amazon's Push to Dominate Black Friday With All-Day Sports
items.summary: Amazon planned a 15-hour run of live events on Black Friday: golf's The Skins Game, its fourth NFL Black Friday game (Broncos v Steelers) and an NBA doubleheader including the Knicks against the Spurs. The sports content sits in front of the paywall, so no subscription or Prime membership is needed. Last year's Black Friday NFL game averaged 16.33 million viewers, up 21% on 2024 and 70% on the first game in 2023, and Amazon sports partnerships head Charlie Neiman said the company wants big exclusive events that matter to a large share of the Prime base, with more golf rights possible 'if it's big enough'.
items.what_it_means: Streamers are turning holidays into owned, free-to-watch sports days built around their commercial calendar.

items.title: Gloucestershire County Cricket Club unveils new 'Bristol Lions' identity to compete in T20 Blast for 2027
items.summary: Gloucestershire County Cricket Club has launched Bristol Lions as a separate T20 identity for its men's and women's teams from the 2027 season, while County Championship and One-Day Cup cricket stays under the Gloucestershire name. The club says the brand came from audience research, market insight and commercial analysis and is meant to reach Bristol sports followers who have not engaged with county cricket. Head of audience development Jenny Hall said the identity allows a step change in ticketing, partnership and commercial potential. This is a club announcement published in SportsPro's announcements section.
items.what_it_means: A heritage club is creating a second, city-facing brand to recruit fans its existing identity was not reaching.

items.title: DEAG lifts nine-month revenue while EBITDA falls 27%
items.summary: German promoter DEAG grew revenue 4.3% to EUR336.8m in the first nine months of 2026, while EBITDA fell 27% to EUR13.8m. It put the profit pressure partly down to developing new event formats and investing in digitalisation and automation, particularly in ticketing. DEAG sold 9.6m tickets in the period, most through its own platforms such as myticket and gigantic.com, and is continuing a buy-and-build strategy after being acquired by Enhanced Group earlier in November.
items.what_it_means: A mid-size promoter is paying now to own its ticketing and new formats, and margins are carrying the cost.

items.title: How the WNBA's First Union Chief Sees Its Billion-Dollar Growth
items.summary: Coquese Washington, the first WNBPA president, told FOS the new collective bargaining agreement fulfils the union's 1998 goal of making the WNBA a full career. Players once earned as little as $15,000 and her first CBA in 1999 lifted the minimum to $25,000; the March deal raises it to $270,000, and the league says it will pay players more than $1 billion in salary through 2032. Washington credits recent metrics showing the league is a viable business, and the piece notes few players now need to play overseas, with offseason leagues like Unrivaled keeping many in the US year-round.
items.what_it_means: Women's basketball is now built on commercial proof points, where early deals relied on belief.

items.title: Auckland to establish four-stadium 'coordinated' network
items.summary: Auckland Council has unanimously approved a Stadium Network Investment Plan that groups the city's four stadiums into a coordinated network, assigning each a role and directing events to the 'venue of best fit'. Eden Park keeps its own governance and its role as the international concert host, with approval for 32 concerts a year, while the upgraded Western Springs Bowl takes a music-first focus and Go Media Stadium and North Harbour Stadium act as sporting hubs. The council says the aim is to strengthen event hosting amid financial pressures.
items.what_it_means: Cities under financial pressure are planning venues as one portfolio and dividing up the event calendar between them.

items.title: Gridiron gridlock: NFL calls shots on US rights spending
items.summary: The SportBusiness Podcast episode covers the big streamers' appetite for sports rights, with the NFL's next domestic contracts described as shaping media companies' decisions while Fifa's US World Cup rights auction continues. It also covers BT's Euro 2028 national sponsorship, which lets it partially keep Wembley branding rights in a departure from the usual clean-site policy, and asks whether Uefa is relaxing its stance on stadium naming rights. This summary is drawn from the episode page only.
items.what_it_means: The NFL's coming renewal is setting the pace for every other US rights negotiation.

items.title: Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026
items.summary: Football Benchmark data shows Bodø/Glimt grew their combined Instagram and TikTok following from about 136,000 to 888,000 between 1 January and 17 November 2026, a 555% rise and the fastest among leading clubs. Chicago Fire FC were second at 205% and Trabzonspor third at 140%. The release links the growth to the Norwegian club's Champions League run, including wins over Manchester City and Atletico de Madrid. It is an agency announcement from Empower Sports published in SportsPro's announcements section.
items.what_it_means: A big competition run can build a small club an international audience fast, which it then has to turn into something commercial.

items.title: Michael Redd: College Football Is the Next Frontier for Team Ownership
items.summary: NBA All-Star turned investor Michael Redd told FOS's Portfolio Players he sees more ownership potential in college football than the NFL, because there are 32 NFL teams but 300-plus college programmes. Deals so far are mostly minority stakes and private credit, such as Utah's deal with Otro Capital and the Big 12's agreement with RedBird Capital Partners. Redd also expects bigger media rights paydays, suggesting the SEC and Big Ten could form their own super league that would attract streamers like Amazon and Netflix.
items.what_it_means: Private capital is looking at college sport as the next ownership market as pro franchise prices climb.

items.title: Sixers Co-Owner Wants Philly's New Arena to Be Worth a Night Out
items.summary: Sixers co-owner David Adelman told FOS that Philadelphia's planned $1.5 billion arena, a 50-50 joint venture between Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment and Comcast Spectacor, should give people a full night out with something to do before, during and after a game or concert. He points to the Braves' Battery and the Patriots' Patriot Place as mixed-use models that also serve surrounding offices and the community. The South Philly arena will house the Sixers, the Flyers and the city's forthcoming WNBA team, which Adelman calls the first purpose-built building for three teams.
items.what_it_means: Owners are planning new arenas around the whole evening out, with the event as one part of it.

items.title: 5 Things We Heard at NWSL Championship Week
items.summary: At NWSL Championship week in Washington, D.C., league and team executives kept returning to stadiums after semifinal scheduling problems largely caused by teams not owning their venues, with the venue-owning Kansas City Current going on to win the title. North Carolina Courage chief business officer Ralph Vuono said tenants do not own most commercial rights, while owners keep concessions, ticketing, parking, merchandise and naming rights in full. Denver Summit FC president Jen Millet said lacking those revenue streams holds back team valuations, and commissioner Jessica Berman said the league is focused on infrastructure it can control or influence.
items.what_it_means: In women's sport, control of the venue is being framed as control of the commercial rights that drive valuations.

items.title: From investment to impact: Lessons from North American sponsorship leaders
items.summary: The Sponsor's roundtables in Toronto and Chicago brought together sponsors including BMO, Bell, Interac, KPMG, Deloitte and Abbott to discuss sponsorship effectiveness. BMO described using decades of soccer investment to engage around a major tournament without being an official sponsor, a difference between buying an association and building one. Sponsors also raised frustration with territorial restrictions on team deals, which clash with social media's lack of borders, and said league-wide deals can bring wastage in markets where a brand has no presence or a competitor holds the local team.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are questioning how much territorial rights are worth when the audience they reach is not bound by geography.

items.title: Promoter Peachtree Entertainment Abruptly Ceases Operations
items.summary: Nashville-based independent promoter Peachtree Entertainment has told agencies and staff it is winding down immediately, after rapid expansion into venues and festivals including Rock The South and Rock The Country. A statement to local media said the company sustained more than $20 million in festival-related losses over the past two years. Pollstar notes Rock The Country faced political backlash this year, with artists pulling out and a stop cancelled, and that Peachtree had not publicly confirmed the news.
items.what_it_means: Festival losses can sink an independent promoter quickly, leaving host cities and venues to pick up the calendar.

items.title: Content, everywhere, all the time: Five sports video consumption trends to watch in 2027
items.summary: Using viewing data from the Canal+-owned Dailymotion network, SportsPro sets out five sports video trends for 2027. Dailymotion's Jennifer Matteucci says live remains the premium anchor, but the fastest growth is in clips, highlights, creator commentary and replays around the event. Mobile leads before live events and around social, connected TV leads for live matches and full replays, and desktop for news and analysis, so the same fan moves across screens through one journey.
items.what_it_means: Rights holders are being urged to treat the whole viewing journey around a live event as one connected product.

items.title: For some brands, humor plus niche targeting is a winning formula
items.summary: At the Brands&Culture conference, Columbia Sportswear's Matt Sutton and goodwipes' Meredith Diehn described pairing humour with niche communities. Columbia's Cannes-winning 'Expedition Impossible' stunt challenged flat-earthers and drew 10 million organic views, and a fax-in Helvetia fleece giveaway sold out online in 15 minutes. Goodwipes, which activates heavily in running, flew a 'Please take a pre-race poop' banner over the TCS New York City Marathon start village.
items.what_it_means: Brands are using humour aimed at tight communities, including at live events, to create wider conversation.

items.title: Megaforce looks to unlock Latam stadium stock for superstars' staging
items.summary: German staging firm Megaforce told IQ its Vega system, debuting in 2027, assembles the roof at stage level and raises it on its own towers, removing the need for cranes. CEO Michael Brombacher says more than 70% of Latin American stadiums do not allow crane access, which has forced some international tours to use smaller setups. The company plans to base the system in the region for half of each year.
items.what_it_means: Venue limitations shape which tours and productions fans in a region actually get to see.

items.title: Belmont Park's total makeover nears its photo finish
items.summary: SBJ toured the remade Belmont Park, a $555 million project with $455 million from New York state, which replaced the old grandstand with a building a third of the size. More than 10 new spaces are self-sufficient for event hosting, making year-round use easier, and the fourth floor will have 32 enclosed private suites. The building will host the 2027 Belmont Stakes and next October's Breeders' Cup.
items.what_it_means: A historic venue has been rebuilt smaller and more premium, with year-round events in mind.

items.title: Kraft Heinz isn't afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
items.summary: Halfway through year one of a five-year global NFL partnership covering Kraft, Velveeta, Philadelphia and Kraft Mac & Cheese, Kraft Heinz is weaving its brands into fan moments in playful ways. Its Thanksgiving weekend activation, Velveeta Pylon Plays, makes US fans eligible to win Velveeta via Uber Eats when a touchdown scorer hits an end-zone pylon, with no branding on the pylons themselves. Heinz also sponsors Prime Video's Red Zone Moments, and the company says Heinz dollar sales rose 20% in the week of its NFL Draft activation compared with the same week in 2025.
items.what_it_means: A portfolio sponsor is tying its brands to in-game moments fans already watch for, and reporting a sales lift from it.

items.title: Dynamo see 20% revenue surge as attendance, partnerships grow
items.summary: Houston Dynamo revenue rose 20% between the 2025 and 2026 seasons, according to President of Business Operations Jessica O'Neill, citing the Houston Business Journal. Dynamo home attendance grew 6% to 18,719 a match and the NWSL's Houston Dash grew 14%, while new national partners included LaCroix, Kroger, Dude Wipes and Higginbotham. O'Neill credits growth in lead generation: the club aimed to double new leads across both teams in 2026 and is on pace to triple them, which fed attendance, digital engagement and community event turnout.
items.what_it_means: A mid-market club tied its revenue growth to building a much larger pipeline of new fan leads.

items.title: Sports Media Pod: Amazon is bringing new advertisers to the NFL
items.summary: On SBJ's Sports Media Podcast, Amazon Ads executive Billy Davis tells Josh Carpenter that Prime Video has attracted 80 brands that had never advertised in the NFL before. He also discusses Amazon bringing new advertisers to the NBA and to its wider sports portfolio.
items.what_it_means: Streaming rights holders are widening the pool of brands buying into live sport, beyond the traditional NFL advertisers.

items.title: NBA Europe formalizes $10.9B fund to infuse future arenas
items.summary: The NBA has created a $10.9B initiative, backed by firms including Apollo Sports Capital, Ares, Arctos, Blackstone, HPS, J.P. Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak, to help future NBA Europe franchises build or renovate arenas and develop mixed-use districts around them. The league has pointed prospective owners to a 2024 Accenture study projecting San Francisco's Chase Center and Thrive City contributed $4.2B to the local economy over five years. Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum called it a 5 to 20 year project that is about enhancing the fan experience, with initial franchises expected to be formalised as soon as Q1 2027.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is treating venues and the districts around them as the core of its European business case.

items.title: Column: College football tailgating is going corporate
items.summary: Summarising Will Leitch in The Athletic, SBJ reports that athletic departments taking control of tailgating spots has become a nationwide trend. RevelXP, founded by a private equity firm to reimagine gameday and non-gameday experiences, now has deals with more than two-thirds of Power 4 schools, and The Grove at Ole Miss is now more than three-quarters vendor based. Leitch argues there is a long-term cost in turning a tradition passed between generations into another revenue line.
items.what_it_means: Monetising fan traditions around the game brings new revenue and a risk of eroding what made them valuable.

items.title: Price cuts drive Corona Capital's 'best year in three years'
items.summary: OCESA's Corona Capital in Mexico City sold 220,000 tickets for its 20-22 November festival, its strongest sales in three years, after cutting ticket prices by 10% and making its first concerted push to sell to American fans. OCESA's Memo Parra says the cut was driven by the volume of stadium and arena shows passing through Mexico, framing fans' choice as going to Bruno Mars or the festival. Savings came from many small budget cuts, including catering and crew scheduling, while attendance was roughly level with 2019.
items.what_it_means: Festivals compete with every other big night out for the same fan budget, and some are cutting costs to win it.

items.title: Fanatics sees record year of retail sales for NFL International Games
items.summary: Fanatics says merchandise sales across its NFL Shop city-centre and stadium stores for the International Games season rose more than 40% on 2025, across eight games in six countries including first regular-season games in Melbourne, Rio de Janeiro and Paris. More than 250,000 fans visited NFL stores, and Munich set the record for single game-day sales at a European NFL game. Online NFL merchandise sales through Fanatics' channels rose 17% across London's three game weeks.
items.what_it_means: International games are working as retail events that reach fans well beyond the stadium.

items.title: U.S. Ski & Snowboard carrying commercial momentum into domestic FIS events
items.summary: U.S. Ski & Snowboard is hosting a record 14 FIS World Cups this season, more than double four years ago, with more than 20 sponsors including a new Dick's Sporting Goods deal. CEO Sophie Goldschmidt says home events give brands more chances to activate and meet fans, and that the brand is becoming more aspirational and lifestyle-led to reach casual fans. NBC will air every alpine World Cup race, and USSS and FIS are launching a YouTube and FAST channel, alongside a second Togethxr merch collaboration, 'Everyone Watches Women's Skiing'.
items.what_it_means: A national governing body is growing sponsorship by hosting more home events and courting casual fans.

items.title: NWSL Championship is league's second-best audience yet, but down 6% from 2025
items.summary: CBS averaged 1.12 million viewers for the KC Current's NWSL championship win over the Washington Spirit, down 6% on last year's record 1.18 million but the league's second-best audience. Women 21 and older made up 47% of the audience, its largest ever in that demo, up from 42%. The postseason averaged 610,000 viewers over six telecasts, up 11% on 2025, after regular-season viewership fell 19% ahead of the final year of current rights deals in 2027.
items.what_it_means: The NWSL's big moments are holding audience while regular-season viewing softens ahead of a rights renewal.

items.title: Essence Festival Officially Leaving New Orleans
items.summary: The Essence Festival of Music and Culture, one of the largest Black festivals in the US, is leaving New Orleans after more than three decades, officials confirmed to Pollstar. Negotiations between the city and festival leaders stalled over contracts and vendor payments, and the city's contract expired in September. Organiser Sundial Media Group said the festival generated more than $300 million in economic impact for New Orleans and Louisiana in 2025.
items.what_it_means: Major festivals are portable assets, and host cities can lose them when the partnership terms break down.

items.title: Netflix continues NFL evolution with start to Thanksgiving tentpole window
items.summary: Netflix and the NFL are launching Thanksgiving Eve football with Rams v Packers, pitched as a new holiday tradition for a night when people go out and reconnect. Netflix is working with EverPass, DAZN for Business and DirecTV for Business to get the game into bars and restaurants, while sources say at-home TV usage that night is no lower than a typical November Wednesday. U2 plays halftime, and Netflix already has four games set for 2027, including a Thanksgiving Eve return.
items.what_it_means: Streamers are creating new holiday windows and taking them to the venues where people gather, beyond the living room.

items.title: Data drive: Ally report shows fan spending on women's sports grows
items.summary: Ally has released its second Cost of Fandom report, finding fan spending on women's sports rising and narrowing the gap with men's sports, where spending held steady at $950. Gen Z is driving the growth, putting 34% of its sports spending into women's sports, compared with 13% for Boomers.
items.what_it_means: Younger fans are directing a much larger share of their sports wallet to women's sport than older fans do.

items.title: 'Our category felt dusty': Why Strauss now spends a third of its marketing budget on sponsorship
items.summary: German workwear brand Strauss ended its sponsorship of the German national team at the end of 2025 and in September became UEFA's first official referee partner, adding to its Europa League and Conference League deals. Chief executive Henning Strauss says the brand no longer needs to buy awareness at home and is shifting budget to growth markets such as the UK, Australia and North America. Sponsorship now accounts for about a third of a marketing budget he puts at a few hundred million euros, and he acknowledges the referee deal carries some risk given fans' views of VAR.
items.what_it_means: A challenger brand is using sport sponsorship to buy relevance in new markets rather than defend awareness it already owns.

items.title: Podcast palooza and other NWSL championship takeaways
items.summary: Around the NWSL Championship in Washington, D.C., digital media properties brought their online audiences together in person, with Just Women's Sports and Men in Blazers both holding paid live podcast recordings to sold-out crowds, presented by Amazon Prime and CarMax respectively. Shows linked to Togethxr, iHeartRadio, Vox Media and Footballco were also on site, including at the Ally House space and the league's Fan Fest. JWS chief executive Haley Rosen says championship weekend can now be the centrepiece of sponsorship packages after years of convincing brands.
items.what_it_means: Media brands are turning a league's marquee weekend into paid live events and sponsor inventory of their own.

items.title: Super Bowl LXI Coming to IMAX As Disney Expands Distribution
items.summary: ESPN, the NFL and IMAX have agreed to show Super Bowl LXI live in hundreds of US IMAX cinemas on 14 February 2027, a first for the game, plus select international markets including Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. It will be the largest live event in IMAX's history. Disney says it wants to reach fans across an unprecedented range of platforms, adding to an already wide set of viewing options.
items.what_it_means: The biggest broadcast in sport is being sold as a ticketed out-of-home experience as well as a TV event.

items.title: NWSL regular season viewership dropped 19%, but early playoff figures were up
items.summary: NWSL regular-season viewership fell 19% across ESPN, ABC, ESPN2, ION and CBS, with 98 measured matches averaging about 173,000 viewers after 20 games were added to the inventory. Adults 18-34 made up 11.1% of the audience, the best share under the current deals. Quarterfinal and semifinal playoff games averaged 494,000, up 13%, with 18-34 viewers up 95%, and the league has one season left on its national deals, with IMG advising on talks.
items.what_it_means: More inventory diluted the average audience, while marquee games and younger viewers grew ahead of a rights negotiation.

items.title: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL Valuations Outpace Surge in American Wealth
items.summary: A J.P. Morgan report finds big four franchise valuations have compounded at about 12% a year since 2000, ahead of the S&P 500 (about 6.8%) and the top 0.1% wealth bracket (7.3%), driven mainly by scarcity, with only four teams added between 2000 and 2025. The number of US billionaires rose from 243 to 902 between 2002 and 2025, but rising valuations have narrowed the pool able to buy control of a team alone.
items.what_it_means: Scarcity keeps pushing team values beyond what single owners can fund, shaping who buys and how.

items.title: Inside Hershey's push for movie magic
items.summary: Hershey, a film about Milton Hershey that took about five years to produce, is the latest brand and entertainment crossover, with the company involved in scriptwriting, holding veto rights over casting and having staff on set every day. An executive says it is not a 90-minute commercial. Alongside the release, Hershey is bringing back five-cent pricing for one day on 25 November and rolling out vintage packaging.
items.what_it_means: Brands are moving from sponsoring entertainment to producing it, with retail tie-ins around the release.

items.title: Top Tours: Ed Sheeran's 'Loop Tour' Grosses More Than $120M In North America
items.summary: Ed Sheeran finished the North American leg of his Loop Tour with a sold-out stadium show in Tampa on 7 November, adding $120.6 million to the tour's gross according to figures reported to Pollstar. The 2026 world tour now stands at $232.6 million from just under 1.9 million tickets across 49 concerts, with a Latin American stadium run to finish by 11 December.
items.what_it_means: Stadium touring by a single global act continues to generate sport-scale box office.

items.title: SailGP Adds UAE Team as It Enters New Era of Private Ownership
items.summary: SailGP is adding a 14th franchise, representing the United Arab Emirates, the first in the league's era of fully independent team ownership after eight years of overhauling its model. The team is majority owned by former Vitol executive Chris Bake, with Mubadala Capital taking a minority stake and SailGP retaining a share. The UAE hosted two stops this season, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
items.what_it_means: A newer league is using host markets and outside investors to build franchise value.

items.title: NBA off to best viewership yet for non-lockout season, buoyed by young demo increases
items.summary: In year two of its new media rights setup, the NBA is averaging 2.62 million viewers across NBC, ESPN, Prime Video and NBA TV, its best non-lockout season pace on record and up 37% on the same point last season. The Emirates NBA Cup is averaging 2 million viewers on Prime Video, up 90%, while viewers aged 18-34 are up 50% and 12-17 are up 57%, and about 25% of national TV viewers are now under 35. Live game and content viewing across the NBA App and League Pass is up 50%, the Tap to Watch effort drove 8 million live streams in the first month, and local games are up 24% across a mix of over-the-air, RSN and streaming deals.
items.what_it_means: Spreading games across broadcast and streaming partners is coinciding with a younger, larger national audience for the NBA.

items.title: Meta inks 49ers sponsorship, will give away AI glasses
items.summary: The 49ers have signed Meta to a multiyear partnership in a new category, 'official moment maker', centred on its AI glasses. The launch activation gives Oakley Meta HSTN glasses, which usually sell for $399 or more, to more than 4,700 suite holders and club season ticket holders for the franchise's 80th anniversary. WhatsApp becomes the team's official instant messenger provider to support its marketing in the UK, UAE and Mexico under the NFL's global markets programme, and Meta also presents the Salute to Service campaign and gets digital signage at Levi's Stadium.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are buying categories built around fan behaviour, putting product in the hands of a team's most valuable ticket holders.

items.title: NFL's Hans Schroeder: More big changes coming to sports rights market
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers event, NFL chief media officer Hans Schroeder said more consolidation and ownership changes are likely among rights holders, after two of the league's seven live game partners were part of major transactions in 2026, and that sports content has never been more valuable. On the same stage, Bank of America analyst Jessica Reif Ehrlich predicted Walmart would be big in sports rights acquisitions in 2027. Schroeder also said he is preparing for the pay-TV universe to bottom out, which MoffettNathanson puts at about 50 million households in 2030, and ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said ESPN would like World Series rights when Fox's deal ends after 2028.
items.what_it_means: The buyers of sports rights are changing, with retailers named alongside media companies and the pay-TV bundle nearing a floor.

items.title: Pinehurst, Titleist seeing early returns on new retail location
items.summary: The Titleist Shop at Pinehurst Resort, the first location of its kind in the US, opened in autumn 2025 next to the driving range, a departure from Titleist's usual reliance on big-box stores and pro shops. With 450,000 to 500,000 rounds a year at the resort, it has printed custom logos on more than 2,000 dozen balls, sold more than 600 Scotty Cameron putters and nearly 500 Vokey wedges, and lifted club fittings from about 200 a year to more than 700 by mid-November. Pinehurst's Eric Kuester compares it to an Apple store, and the resort keeps all the revenue.
items.what_it_means: A venue that already hosts the fan's experience can turn a sponsor into an on-site store, with exclusives that only work in that place.

items.title: How Trackhouse Racing helps VIPs talk to cars, literally
items.summary: NASCAR team Trackhouse Racing built an app for guests in its pit box that sends race updates from a persona of Connor Zilisch's No. 88 car, called 88Bot, drawn from race-day data. The team hosts 30 to 60 VIPs a race, including families, partners and prospective sponsors, and owner Justin Marks said technology has become a mandate in the business to make the guest experience as vital as the racing. Trackhouse worked with digital design firm Very Good Ventures from mid-2024, testing in the few hours before each race and handling roughly 25,000 data messages a second.
items.what_it_means: Teams are using their own live data to make hospitality more valuable for partners and prospective sponsors.

items.title: PGA Tour Fall Ends With Ticket Fiasco After Weather Disruption
items.summary: Heavy rain cancelled Saturday play at the RSM Classic at Sea Island, pushing the third round to Sunday and the final round to Monday. Saturday tickets, from $65 general admission to nearly $600 for the Skybox Club, were not honoured on Sunday and no fans were allowed in on Monday, with organisers citing safe capacity and limited volunteers. Fans learned through social media that refunds were not on offer, comments on the tournament's post were turned off, and organisers later said they would contact Saturday ticket holders directly.
items.what_it_means: When an event is disrupted, the refund and communication policy becomes the fan experience, and silence on social compounds the damage.

items.title: Canada's TD Coliseum celebrates 'tremendous' first year post-$300m renovation
items.summary: Oak View Group's TD Coliseum in Hamilton, Ontario, drew more than 850,000 fans to 110 events in its first year after a C$300 million renovation, with acts including Cardi B, Smashing Pumpkins and Katseye. The 18,000-capacity arena, about 70km from Toronto, added a rigging grid, acoustic panelling, a bigger open floor, premium suites and a purpose-built artist compound. Pollstar's mid-year rankings put it as the top-selling venue in the Canadian market, and 75% of ticket buyers came from outside the Hamilton area.
items.what_it_means: A rebuilt arena outside a major city can pull most of its audience from elsewhere, if it is built to win tours.

items.title: Novo signs on as 76ers corporate sponsor
items.summary: Novo, maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, has signed as a 76ers sponsor with presenting rights to an online content series plus social, digital and arena signage. Activation includes a 'First Step Sweepstakes' where fans pledge to complete healthy activities for a chance to win Sixers experiences and merchandise. Novo has been quiet in US sports apart from a cycling team, the Hurricanes and UNC, and the 76ers have signed more than a dozen new sponsors out of 23 during their resurgence.
items.what_it_means: A new category of sponsor is entering US sport through content and fan participation rather than signage alone.

items.title: How Joya Studio brought the scents of A24's 'Backrooms' into consumers' own rooms
items.summary: Fragrance house Joya Studio released a 'scent score' for A24's Backrooms, five bespoke smells designed to be sprayed at set timestamps while watching at home, plus a candle of the final scent. It launched as the film moved into its streaming window at the end of September, giving viewers a reason to revisit a film that has taken $400 million worldwide, A24's biggest success. Preorders sold out quickly.
items.what_it_means: Entertainment brands are designing products that make the at-home window an event in its own right.

items.title: Sanjay Govil is taking a big swing at cricket in the U.S.
items.summary: Washington Freedom owner Sanjay Govil, one of several tech founders backing Major League Cricket alongside Satya Nadella and Shantanu Narayen, says around 40 million people watch cricket in the US. The league is building its own grounds, including Pomona, California, which will host Olympic cricket in 2028, and a Frederick, Maryland pitch opening next year as the league grows from six to eight teams. Govil said the month-long season needs to expand, awareness has lagged, and the right media deal should be measured by accessibility as well as money.
items.what_it_means: A new league with an existing diaspora audience is prioritising venues, a longer season and reach before rights fees.

items.title: K.C. Current's first NWSL title rewards ownership's infrastructure investment
items.summary: The Kansas City Current beat the Washington Spirit 2-1 at Audi Field in front of a sellout crowd of 19,365 to win their first NWSL title, after a postseason marked by venue availability and field condition problems. The Current's owners, Angie and Chris Long with Brittany and Patrick Mahomes, built the league's first purpose-built training facility and stadium, and Angie Long said the building gives the team permanence and relevance that lays a foundation of value beyond direct revenue. A home team in a predetermined final drove a record $400 get-in price two hours before kickoff, and the open Fan Fest at The Wharf made 14 brand activations, including presenting sponsor Google Pixel, accessible to passers-by as well as ticket holders.
items.what_it_means: In women's sport, owning the venue is being framed as a source of franchise value and fan relevance, as well as a way to secure dates.

items.title: NFL's Mexico City Finale Could Break International Viewership Record
items.summary: The 49ers play the Vikings in Mexico City on NBC's Sunday Night Football, the last of nine NFL international games this season and the league's first in Mexico City since 2022. The record for a game played outside the US is 24.9 million viewers for Cowboys-Ravens in Rio de Janeiro on CBS, while Patriots-Lions in Munich drew 12.15 million on Fox, the best Sunday morning window result for an international game. League leaders have said they may go to 10 international games next season and could eventually reach 16, and NFL EVP Peter O'Reilly said the owners also discussed growing international media and sponsor partnerships, global and local.
items.what_it_means: The NFL is scaling international games as a domestic TV product and a platform for global and local sponsorship at the same time.

items.title: Madkour: League leaders face varying inflection points
items.summary: Abraham Madkour's column looks at three leagues at different moments: incoming MLS commissioner Larry Berg, who emphasises speed and the product; MLB's labour talks, where a salary cap and floor could change the look of the sport with fewer games and bigger tentpole events; and the PGA Tour under Brian Rolapp. Rolapp argued that media rights are finite and the best product will get fan and commercial attention, and said the Tour's spring and summer schedule is an advantage because the fall's gross rating points go to college football, the NFL and the World Series. He pitched summer as a strong window for advertisers and for streamers trying to reduce subscriber churn.
items.what_it_means: Leagues are positioning their calendar around when rivals are absent, selling the quiet months to advertisers and streamers.

items.title: Chiefs consider PSL fees to help fund new $3B stadium
items.summary: Citing the Kansas City Star, SBJ reports that newly signed agreements for the Chiefs' $3B domed stadium in Wyandotte County, Kansas, show the team is at least considering personal seat licences to help fund its 40% private share, with public funds covering the other 60%. It is the first public sign the team is evaluating the fees, although season-ticket holder surveys have asked about PSLs, and chair and CEO Clark Hunt said no decision has been made. Arrowhead has never used PSLs, but a growing number of NFL teams building new stadiums use them for upfront funding.
items.what_it_means: New stadium builds keep shifting part of the construction bill onto existing season-ticket holders, which tests how far fan loyalty can be monetised up front.

items.title: Disney Rolls Out New Perks and Membership Tiers For Fan Club Membership
items.summary: D23, Disney's official fan club, is adding a new $39.99 Gold Access tier for 2027 between its free general membership and the paid Gold Essential, Choice and Complete plans, which range up to $329.99 a year. The free tier includes the newsletter and sweepstakes, while Gold Access is needed for Gold events, discounts and early ticket access to some events. Higher tiers add a membership kit and choices such as pin sets, Fandango tickets, gift memberships or a plus-one event pass, ahead of Disney's first D23 Asia convention and a 2027 calendar of anniversary events.
items.what_it_means: Disney is widening its fan club ladder with a cheaper paid entry tier above free, so more fans can move from newsletter to paying member.

items.title: Women's Sports Have Gotten Too Big for Small Stadiums
items.summary: Several contending WNBA and NWSL teams hit venue clashes this postseason: the WNBA moved three Finals games so the Atlanta Dream could play in the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena instead of their 3,500-seat home, and the NWSL's top three seeds all faced conflicts at stadiums they do not own. NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said the league needs to prioritise venues it can control or influence, through ownership, shared ownership with MLS teams or partnerships that put the tenant first. The Golden State Valkyries, who share owners with the Warriors and Chase Center, had a Doja Cat concert moved, and arenas like the United Center write contingency dates into event contracts during playoff windows.
items.what_it_means: Women's teams that do not control their venue are losing their biggest commercial moments to calendar clashes, which is pushing leagues toward owner groups with buildings.

items.title: At this year's NWSL championship, sponsors are putting athletes first
items.summary: NWSL sponsors are building their championship weekend activations around players. Google Pixel, presenting sponsor of the NWSL playoffs and championship for three seasons, also sponsors the NWSL Players Association and runs a Players Lab where NWSL, USWNT and WNBA athletes test its wearables; Google's Kate Johnson said women's sports audiences 'pay you back' and are very loyal. CarMax CMO Sarah Lane said the brand wanted the partnership to be about more than a logo on signage, and its championship skills challenge has grown from a fan clinic into a player-led event.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors in women's sport are buying access to athletes and their channels, alongside the league inventory, to reach fans.

items.title: Brewers break World Series merch sales record and aren't slowing down
items.summary: Citing the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, SBJ reports the Brewers sold more merchandise after their World Series win than during the entire 2026 season and set an in-venue World Series merchandise record, 9% above the 2022 Astros. Business president Rick Schlesinger said team store traffic is 10 to 15 times a normal day and 90% of what is selling is postseason gear. The club does not budget for the postseason, but its 2027 ticket sales projections are at or above franchise records.
items.what_it_means: A title run creates a short, outsized buying window, and the club is using it to read demand for the next regular season.

items.title: WWE's Nick Khan breaks down Netflix, ESPN deals, eyes continued global growth
items.summary: On Bloomberg's 'The Deal', WWE president Nick Khan said the 10-year, $5B Netflix deal came together quickly because Netflix needed subscriber growth and was entering ad-supported streaming, and 52 weeks of WWE programming gave it a fuller slate to sell advertisers. On ESPN, he said 'you can't speak to your consumers like they're inside the boardroom with you', so WWE had wrestlers make videos telling fans where to watch, pushed through its 600 million social followers. He also said WWE cannot simply pipe American content overseas and needs to be on the ground internationally.
items.what_it_means: Year-round live programming is valuable to streamers building ad businesses, and the rights holder still carries the job of telling fans where to find it.

items.title: Investment deals aren't slowing down in sports
items.summary: SBJ's wrap of its Dealmakers conference reports investors still see franchises as attractive for durable revenue and scarcity, alongside a boom in stadiums and mixed-use real estate. Marquee Development's Megan Cantwell said the Gallagher Way district beside Wrigley Field runs more than 300 events a year and drives a million incremental visitors outside game day, beating revenue expectations with lifts in sponsorship and retail. Muse Capital's Assia Grazioli-Venier said women's sports properties that are good at collecting data and understanding their fandom have a lucrative opportunity.
items.what_it_means: Investors are valuing sports properties on what they earn from fans and venues across the whole year, beyond the fixture list.

items.title: Record demand drives early hospitality sellouts for 2027 Tour Championship
items.summary: Citing Simply Buckhead, SBJ reports several premium hospitality offerings at the PGA Tour's 2027 Tour Championship at East Lake have already sold out, the earliest sellouts in the event's history. The demand comes as companies invest in experiences to connect with clients, partners and employees, and as 2027 is the last year at East Lake before the event moves to a matchplay format on a rotation of courses in 2028.
items.what_it_means: Corporate hospitality demand is strongest where an event feels scarce or final.

items.title: Players Era Festival sees rapid growth continuing after biggest event yet
items.summary: Citing USA Today, SBJ reports the Players Era Festival has become college basketball's biggest regular-season event three years after launch, with a multiyear ESPN deal and a record 24 teams, up from 18, and organisers turning teams away. Backing from RedBird-linked EverWonder helped secure MGM as host, and NIL opportunities drew coaches in. The same roundup cites Adweek reporting that Disney Advertising has more than 20 college basketball sponsors, seven of them new.
items.what_it_means: A new made-for-media event can grow fast when it bundles a venue, a broadcaster and a reason for teams to show up.

items.title: New Balance extends Ohtani through rest of playing career
items.summary: New Balance has extended its sponsorship of Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani through the rest of his playing career and is renaming its innovation facility the Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab. Citing GQ, SBJ says it appears to be the first deal to cover exclusively a star's playing days and the first of its kind in MLB.
items.what_it_means: Brands are locking up global athlete relationships for the long term, before the next renewal becomes a bidding war.

items.title: NWSL, PWHL Holding Off on Prediction-Market Deals
items.summary: The NWSL and PWHL told Front Office Sports they are not pursuing prediction-market partnerships, while the NBA, NHL, MLB and MLS each have between one and four with platforms such as Kalshi, Polymarket, DraftKings and Novig. NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said the league is evaluating the category given scrutiny and unsettled regulation. The NFL is also a holdout, while Polymarket has signed the Bundesliga, LaLiga and Serie A.
items.what_it_means: Some leagues are choosing to leave a fast-growing sponsorship category unsold while its regulation is contested.

items.title: UBS Arena marks five years with efforts to keep evolving
items.summary: Citing Newsday, SBJ reports that five years after opening, UBS Arena is becoming part of a wider campus with the rebuilt Belmont Park racetrack and Belmont Park Village shopping. An Islanders ticket can be used at the racetrack on game days, and purchases at the village can be delivered to the arena for pickup. Business president Kelly Cheeseman said the job now is to build a broader experience, and the arena competes with Barclays Center and Madison Square Garden for concerts.
items.what_it_means: Arenas are being run as destinations that bundle sport, concerts, retail and other attractions around one visit.

items.title: In new ticketing model, NFL aims for more Rolex, less T.J. Maxx
items.summary: NFL club business executives Schuyler Simpson and Bobby Gallo say the league's Ticketing 3.0 platform, powered by Ticketmaster under a seven-year deal, aims to personalise ticket buying around each fan's habits and history, with a launch hoped for before the 2027 schedule release in May. Bringing more transactions into the official ecosystem gives the league more fan data, which it wants to share across partners such as Uber, Marriott and Amazon in a connected 'ring' rather than the current hub-and-spoke model. The league wants fans to go straight to NFL.com instead of searching for tickets, and Gallo said owning its own ticketing platform remains possible in the long term.
items.what_it_means: The NFL is treating ticket buying as the front door to a shared fan data asset that adds value for every league partner.

items.title: Top MLB promotions of 2026: Hot giveaways drew fans to ballparks
items.byline: David Broughton and Emma Grace Patrick
items.summary: SBJ's analysis of every MLB club's promotional schedule counted more than 10.6 million game-day giveaways in 2026 and more than 5,000 activations in total, with bobbleheads handed out at a record 204 games. About 20% of the 71.8 million fans who attended received a souvenir, sponsors put their logo on 72% of giveaways, and 44% of all promotions were sponsored. Specialty-ticket packages rose 31% on 2025 to 1,496, led by college-themed packages, and IP brands such as Hello Kitty activated at a record 240 games.
items.what_it_means: Baseball clubs are leaning harder on themed, sponsored reasons to attend, which turns the matchday itself into a sponsor and ticket product.

items.title: PWHL expands Takeover Tour to 19 North American markets
items.summary: The PWHL will take 24 games to 19 markets outside its teams' home cities this season in its most expansive Takeover Tour yet, with Halifax hosting three games and Denver, Philadelphia and Washington, D.C. two each. The aim is to put the league in front of more people and test the waters for future expansion, and every city has been in the expansion conversation at some point. Most games will be played in NHL buildings, starting at Capital One Arena on 2 January.
items.what_it_means: A women's league is using touring neutral-site games to build demand and gather evidence in markets before it commits to expansion.

items.title: Verizon renews LaLiga sponsorship amid World Cup years
items.summary: Verizon has renewed its sponsorship of LaLiga in the US and Canada under a new multiyear deal, its second renewal since the partnership began in 2019-20, and LaLiga North America says it is their largest agreement yet. Verizon is also hosting sweepstakes that give fans access to the league, a tactic it carried over from its NFL and World Cup work. LaLiga North America's Nicolas Garcia Hemme said brands that activate experientially, rather than only through marks or media buys, help the league grow fandom.
items.what_it_means: A sponsor is backing a foreign league's growth in the US between two World Cups, betting on soccer fandom that it can help build through fan access.

items.title: Mark Walter Sought $800M for Record-Breaking Sparks Sale
items.summary: New Padres owners Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones are on the verge of buying the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks from Mark Walter for about $750 million, according to Front Office Sports sources, after Walter initially asked for $800 million. The deal, first reported by Sportico, would shatter the previous WNBA record for a majority control sale of $300 million.
items.what_it_means: The price of a WNBA franchise has more than doubled its previous record, a sign of how buyers now value women's sport as a commercial asset.

items.title: Sports Media Pod: The Pat McAfee Effect -- ESPN's younger audience has doubled
items.summary: On SBJ's Sports Media Podcast, ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro defends Pat McAfee's impact on College GameDay, pointing to more than 100% growth among viewers aged 18 to 24 over four years. He explains why McAfee's energy, humour and connection with younger fans support ESPN's top long-term priority of expanding its audience.
items.what_it_means: ESPN is backing a personality to recruit younger viewers, treating audience growth as more important than protecting a traditional format.

items.title: ATP approves combining commercial assets into ATP Ventures, increasing player compensation
items.summary: The ATP Board and ATP Media shareholders unanimously approved ATP Ventures, which will bring ATP Media, Tennis Data Innovations and the tour's central sponsorship activity under one roof for the first time, aiming to start in 2028. The move is designed to speed up commercial growth and improve the experience for fans and for media, data and sponsor partners. The ATP also approved measures to lift total player compensation above $350 million from 2028.
items.what_it_means: Men's tennis is consolidating media, data and sponsorship into one commercial vehicle so partners can buy the tour as a single package.

items.title: Mammoth, Avalanche set combined Winter Classic merch record on Fanatics sites
items.summary: Fanatics says Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche Winter Classic merchandise set a combined record in the first 24 hours after launch, at more than double the previous best Winter Classic launch. Both teams also passed the previous best-selling NHL jersey launch day, and eight of the top 10 selling products across all teams and leagues on Fanatics sites were for the Winter Classic.
items.what_it_means: A one-off event with its own look can drive record merchandise demand across a league's whole retail network.

items.title: NFL's Mexico fan base surges despite game hiatus ahead of 49ers-Vikings matchup
items.summary: NFL Mexico managing director Arturo Olive says the league's Mexican fan base has grown from about 10 million to 40 million over 18 years, even without a regular-season game there since 2022, and the NFL now trails only soccer in total fans. The league has invested heavily in flag football, which has about 4 million players, and signed an agreement with Mexico's federal sports agency to expand it in public schools. The 49ers, who hold NFL marketing rights in Mexico, are running fan events in Mexico City ahead of Sunday's game.
items.what_it_means: The NFL grew a market fourfold through year-round grassroots work, with the games themselves as occasional peaks.

items.title: Berman: NWSL using 2027 Challenge Cup to test Austin as expansion market
items.summary: NWSL Commissioner Jessica Berman announced the 2027 Challenge Cup will be played at Q2 Stadium in Austin, a non-NWSL market, which she framed as a chance to learn the fan base and test appetite for a potential expansion team. It is the second straight Challenge Cup at a neutral site, after Columbus hosted in 2026 before being awarded a $205 million expansion franchise. The league has added four teams since 2024, with two more due in 2028.
items.what_it_means: Women's leagues are using one-off events to measure demand in a market before selling it an expansion team.

items.title: Michael Rapino talks Live Nation's AI strategy, subscription ambitions for 14m-member All Access program, plus 3 other things to know from the firm's 2026 Investor Presentation
items.summary: At Live Nation's 2026 investor presentation, touring president Omar Al-Joulani said the year-old All Access fan membership programme already has 14 million members, who went to 34% more shows than they did over the previous three years. He said Live Nation is using its data and AI with All Access to sell more of its 20 million empty seats, and Michael Rapino called it a quiet little club with a big story over time as a membership subscription business. Rapino also said Live Nation will not hand its checkout or ticket inventory to AI platforms, and the company set a target of 33 million fans through its venues by 2031, up from 11 million.
items.what_it_means: The biggest promoter in live entertainment is treating a direct fan membership as a growth engine to fill unsold seats, and it is keeping that relationship and checkout to itself.

items.title: Vice City-themed night draws new fans to Heat game
items.summary: SBJ's roundup of local coverage says thousands of fans queued in heavy rain outside Kaseya Center for the Heat's GTA VI themed night against the Bucks. Figures provided by the Heat and reported by WPLG's Will Manso show more than 80% of ticket buyers were first-time buyers, and over 20% of those first-timers lived more than 250 miles away. Of fans who bought Vice City merchandise, 95% were first-time buyers at the team store, and over 30% of first-time orders were international.
items.what_it_means: Borrowing a bigger fandom from outside sport brought a largely new set of buyers to a regular-season game, which is the hard part of growing an audience.

items.title: Raiders give fans all access with new TikTok Live show
items.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders became the first NFL team to host an original pregame show on TikTok Live and have now run three episodes of Raiders All Access. The team's senior director of digital content strategy, Gavin Rivera, said the show was made for people outside Raiders fandom and even football fandom, using TikTok-native hosts and pop culture over analysis. The first episode, with an influencer interviewing Ice Cube, drew more than 220,000 unique viewers by the team's count, and the Raiders plan a show for every home game with potential sponsors later.
items.what_it_means: Teams are building shoulder programming specifically for people who are not yet fans, using platforms and hosts those people already follow.

items.title: Ally extends deals with popular women's sports platforms 'Welcome to the Party' and 'The RE-CAP Show'
items.summary: Ally has signed multiyear, multimillion-dollar extensions with the women's soccer platforms Welcome to the Party, hosted by Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy, and The RE-CAP Show, hosted by Tobin Heath and Christen Press. Ally has backed both since their origins and helped produce their first live shows, and RE-CAP grew listeners 47.1% and WTTP 154.5% from 2025 to 2026. Ally will be presenting sponsor of each flagship show, and in April it hit its 2022 pledge to split paid media equally between women's and men's sport, a year early.
items.what_it_means: A sponsor that backed women's sport media early is renewing on platforms it helped build, buying into the fan conversation around the game as well as the game itself.

items.title: LPGA Working With PGA Tour, Networks for Better TV Windows
items.summary: LPGA commissioner Craig Kessler said growth next year centres on collaborating with the PGA Tour and playing more events in network broadcast windows. The LPGA will have at least eight weekend slots on CBS or NBC directly after PGA Tour coverage in 2027, double this season, to benefit from the lead-in. Viewership this season was up 7% across all networks but flat on Golf Channel, and Kessler said fans who browse network channels discover the LPGA and tune in.
items.what_it_means: For a property still building its audience, a better slot on free-to-air network TV can be worth more than a bigger rights fee.

items.title: Dealmakers: Investors see sports' next growth wave beyond team ownership
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers conference, investors from CVC, Muse Capital, Shamrock Capital and Goldman Sachs said the next growth wave lies in revenue streams built around teams, leagues and premium events. Steven Justman described an almost insatiable demand for premium live experiences, and Muse's Assia Grazioli called the female fan a very lucrative one to tap into. CVC's Marc Allera said the business of sport is immature relative to other media categories, with runway in media, sponsorship, hospitality, consumer products, real estate and direct fan relationships.
items.what_it_means: Institutional money increasingly values sport for the live experiences and fan relationships around the team, which raises the bar for how properties monetise them.

items.title: Scarcity, contracted revenue drive rising sports franchise values
items.summary: At SBJ's Dealmakers conference, Monumental's Zach Leonsis, Arctos co-founder Jordan Solomon and J.P. Morgan's Eric Menell said scarcity, contracted revenue and protective league structures keep franchise values rising, though prices like the Lakers' $12.5B sale are getting harder to finance. Leonsis said about 22 NBA teams had regional sports network partners last year against nine this year, and warned against confusing the decline of linear with where rights value remains. Asked about the biggest risk, Solomon pointed to the fan experience, saying teams are competing with sitting on the couch at home.
items.what_it_means: Even the investors driving record valuations name the in-venue fan experience as the biggest risk, because the couch is the competitor.

items.title: The WNBA's Audience Is Bigger Than Its Headlines
items.summary: Just Women's Sports founder Haley Rosen argues in an opinion piece that TV ratings show how many people watched the WNBA but not how much they care. She says her outlet's WNBA social posts drew 405 million views this season, with 70 players drawing at least 100,000 views and 42 topping one million. She argues coverage focused on a few stars and controversies leads brands to partner with the same few athletes, and says the real signal is where fans spend time between games.
items.what_it_means: Depth of fan engagement across many players points brands to a wider set of partnership options than TV ratings and star-led coverage suggest.

items.title: Bills, Sabres leverage venues to make Buffalo a major event destination
items.summary: SBJ's clip of Buffalo News reporting says the Bills and Sabres have made attracting major events to their venues part of their business plan. KeyBank Center is expected to host 193 events and draw 1.4 million people this year, and the new Highmark Stadium opens with six concerts in 2027 including Morgan Wallen, Zach Bryan, Metallica, Noah Kahan and Kenny Chesney. Business president Pete Guelli hopes the momentum leads to an NHL Stadium Series game in 2028 and the NFL Draft in 2029 or 2030.
items.what_it_means: Team owners are treating their venues as year-round event businesses, which makes concerts and tentpole events part of the sports franchise's commercial model.

items.title: Vivid Seats Hands Lenders 80% of Its Stock in $232M Debt Deal
items.summary: Vivid Seats agreed a recapitalisation with lenders that cuts its net debt by about $232 million of the $342 million it owes, adds $60 million in new financing and extends loan maturities to 2032. In return a lender group will own about 80% of the common stock, leaving existing shareholders with 20%. FOS reports the resale marketplace has been squeezed by pricing and inventory pressure from competitors and AI, debt, regulation and its own missteps, and its market value is around $29 million against nearly $2 billion at its 2021 listing.
items.what_it_means: The ticket resale middle layer is under real financial strain, as competition, regulation and AI pressure the economics of reselling access to live events.

items.title: Cowboys' home-field advantage questioned as opposing fans take over AT&T Stadium
items.summary: SBJ's roundup of Dallas columnists describes 49ers fans filling AT&T Stadium for Sunday's 46-40 Cowboys loss, with 'Let's go Niners' chants and Cowboys players booed in warmups. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Mac Engel called it awkward and embarrassing but very profitable, noting a sellout is a sellout and that the Cowboys will not block resale the way some teams do. Jerry Jones said the club had known for weeks how many tickets 49ers fans were buying. The Dallas Morning News' Tim Cowlishaw argued modern US fans are more loyal to individuals and more willing to shift between teams than the home-club fans of the past.
items.what_it_means: A full stadium and a home crowd are different things, and a team that sells to whoever buys can bank the revenue while losing the atmosphere that makes the ticket worth having.

items.title: Relo Metrics data shows WNBA delivered $608M in sponsor value
items.summary: A Relo Metrics report says the WNBA generated more than $608M in sponsor media value this season, with broadcast value up 62% to $545M, or 90% of the total. The Indiana Fever, the only team with every game on national TV, drove $205M, or 37% of broadcast value, and new partners NBC, NBC Sports and USA Network added $105M. Around 85 brands generated more than $1M each, and financial services and healthcare, worth $123M combined, still have no dominant brand.
items.what_it_means: Women's sport sponsor value is growing fast but sits with the most-televised teams, and some big categories are still open for a brand to own.

items.title: Sports media's next growth phase centers on live events, direct distribution and new IP
items.summary: Panelists at SBJ's Media Innovators event said the next phase of sports media will be driven by new distribution, original storytelling and monetising live experiences. Horizon Sports & Experiences' David Levy called owning and creating live IP the biggest opportunity, combining events with VIP experiences, tickets and sponsorship, and said building an audience and collecting fan data are critical. The Suns and Mercury said reach and ratings have doubled and even tripled since moving to free over-the-air broadcasts with Gray Media, and DAZN's Walker Jacobs said the era of 125 million households paying for regional sports networks is never coming back.
items.what_it_means: As the old pay-TV bundle fades, properties are trading fees for reach and looking to live experiences and direct fan relationships for the next revenue stream.

items.title: Heat ready for 'A Night in Vice City' with plenty of GTA VI promotions
items.summary: The Miami Heat are staging 'A Night in Vice City' at Kaseya Center as a lead-in to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, after more than two years of work with Rockstar Games that started when the team saw its arena in the game's trailer. The night includes a Vice-themed court, jerseys with nods to GTA VI and Travis Scott's Cactus Jack brand, GTA-inspired cars outside the arena, in-game music, and concession stands renamed after fictional GTA fast-food chains. Brand and chief growth officer Jennifer Alvarez called it a crossover bringing gaming and sport together in a new way.
items.what_it_means: Sports teams can borrow the pull of a bigger entertainment moment to reach fans who arrive through gaming and culture rather than basketball.

items.title: PGA Tour's Rolapp dishes on creating more media value, diversifying revenue streams
items.summary: Speaking at SBJ's Dealmakers event, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said the sports business comes down to the product: get the most competitive product and people reward you with time and attention, and the commercial side follows. He said US media rights are a $30B a year business that will keep rising as money moves from scripted programming to live sport, but warned it will not feed everything. Rolapp said the Tour's 47 events had been spread across the calendar in ways fans didn't understand, with diluted fields, and that the 2028 Championship series is designed to create scarcity and more media value.
items.what_it_means: Rising rights money will go to the properties that win fans' time, so scarcity and a clearer product matter more than more inventory.

items.title: NFL's Germany Matchup Makes Case for More Sunday Morning Games
items.summary: Fox drew an average US audience of 12.15 million for the Lions' win over the Patriots in Munich, the largest Sunday morning audience for any NFL game on any network. The game opened a Fox tripleheader that Fox says totalled 10.6 billion minutes of viewing, the most-watched regular-season Sunday on one network in NFL history. FOS says the result adds to the likelihood of Sunday morning becoming a permanent fourth window, which an 18-game season would help support.
items.what_it_means: International games are creating new broadcast inventory at home as well as new fans abroad, which raises the value of the league's schedule.

items.title: Why Geico bet big on a youth sports docuseries
items.summary: Geico's eight-episode docuseries Miles that Matter, now on DAZN, follows Greg Olsen, Luke Kuechly and Jonathan Stewart coaching a Charlotte middle school football team. Geico's VP of integrated marketing and media Kate Jalkut said live games show fans the athlete, and the brand wants to tell more stories about the person. Marketing Brew says the series is part of a storytelling-led era of Geico's sports marketing, aimed at connecting with fans beyond plays and highlights to compete for consideration in insurance, and designed not to be overly branded.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are funding original sports storytelling to earn attention between games, using content as a way into consideration in a crowded category.

items.title: RBC City National Bank renews Golden Knights sponsorship for 10 years
items.summary: RBC City National Bank has renewed its founding Golden Knights sponsorship for 10 years, keeping naming rights to the practice facility through 2037 and expanding its rights across owner Bill Foley's portfolio, including the AHL Silver Knights, IFL Knight Hawks, Foley hotels, wineries and AFC Bournemouth. Terms were not disclosed, but business president John Penhollow called it the team's most lucrative corporate partnership and believes it is the NHL's most valuable practice-facility deal. The Golden Knights do not control naming rights to T-Mobile Arena, which makes the practice facility key inventory.
items.what_it_means: Owners with several properties can sell sponsors a whole portfolio of fans and venues, which can grow a deal beyond what one team could offer.

items.title: TikTok says 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on its platform first
items.summary: TikTok's 2026 Music Impact Report, prepared by Luminate, says 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on TikTok before charting, up from 84% in 2024. Songs that went viral spent an average of eight weeks on the chart against two weeks for those that didn't, and reached a median peak of No. 79 against No. 120. The virality and engagement data in the study was provided by TikTok.
items.what_it_means: Discovery for music now happens largely on one social platform before the charts, which shapes where artists and promoters build demand.

items.title: Alexis Ohanian: Women's sports growth 'still just beginning'
items.summary: Speaking on Bloomberg's The Deal, Reddit co-founder and team owner Alexis Ohanian said US women's sports are in the third or fourth inning and globally still in the first. He said brands are showing a lot of energy but women's sports media is fragmented, with no critical mass yet for a brand that wants to buy into the bigger media story. He said there is not enough inventory for all the brand demand in women's sports.
items.what_it_means: Brand demand for women's sport is running ahead of the media inventory available to buy, which favours whoever builds scale first.

items.title: StubHub data reveals growth, distinct audience for women's sports
items.summary: StubHub's 2026 Trend Report shows demand for women's sports is now six times its 2019 level, while demand for live events overall has grown 1.3 times. Repeat buying is rising, with 62% of women's sports ticket buyers returning this year against 55% last year. Nearly 90% of people who bought WNBA or NWSL tickets since 2021 did not buy tickets to the NBA or MLS.
items.what_it_means: Women's sports leagues are building their own ticket-buying audience rather than borrowing the men's, so the commercial case for them rests on reaching a different customer.

items.title: Ezpeleta: MotoGP valued 'reach before fees' in ESPN deal
items.summary: MotoGP's new two-year deal with ESPN covering the US and Latin America is its first US contract since Liberty Media took over, and deputy chief executive Carlos Ezpeleta says the series valued reach before fees. The short term lets MotoGP gauge an underdeveloped US market before renegotiating for 2029. Its VideoPass subscription stays available in the US, its biggest single VideoPass market, with ESPN providing top-of-funnel access, and success will be measured in eyeballs that Ezpeleta hopes carry over to every revenue stream.
items.what_it_means: For a sport still building a market, a broadcast deal can be bought as distribution to grow fans who later pay through other channels.

items.title: Media Innovators: NHL's centralized production providing teams with long-awaited 'stability'
items.summary: After the Main Street Sports regional networks shut in April, the NHL built its own production arm, and six clubs (Blue Jackets, Blues, Hurricanes, Wild, Ducks and Stars) now have their local games produced by the league. Chief media officer David Proper said clubs can now package broadcast commercial time and integrations with their sponsorship inventory as one system, where the RSN's sales once limited what a team could sell. The league plans shoulder programming across all six teams' broadcasts later in the season.
items.what_it_means: When a team controls its local broadcast alongside its sponsorship, it can sell partners one integrated package instead of competing with its own broadcaster.

items.title: HYBE strikes strategic partnership with CAA covering content, merch, brands, and live experiences
items.summary: HYBE, the company behind BTS, has formed a strategic partnership with CAA covering content, brand partnerships, sports, licensing and merchandising, and live experiences across markets including Korea, Japan, the Americas, China and India. Financial terms and duration were not disclosed, and Deadline reported that CAA will represent HYBE's artists, IP and brands. HYBE chief executive Jason Jaesang Lee said the aim is to extend the reach and value of its artists and IP across content, brands and live experiences.
items.what_it_means: The biggest fandom businesses in music are being packaged as IP across brands, merch and live, with representation built for that whole range.

items.title: PS&E invests in MatchWornShirt, to launch live Pacers, Fever auctions
items.summary: Pacers Sports & Entertainment is part of a $20M investment round in Amsterdam-based MatchWornShirt, alongside 35Ventures, John Terry and Tiesto, and will run live auctions of Pacers, Fever and Gainbridge Fieldhouse memorabilia. Chief commercial officer Joey Graziano described auctions opening when a player checks into a game, with prices moving as the match builds, and extending to items like the net, the chair or concert set lists.
items.what_it_means: Teams are turning the emotional peak of a live game into a real-time commerce moment tied to specific items.

items.title: Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business
items.summary: The WTA has launched its first official merchandise collaboration with Sanrio's Hello Kitty, followed by deals with Togethxr and Monarch Commerce for its first online fan shop next year. Chief brand officer Sarah Swanson said fandom in tennis centres on individual athletes, which has left the tour less room for its own branded products than team sports. She argued merchandise can be the top of the funnel as well as the bottom, with people buying a product they like and then discovering the sport behind it.
items.what_it_means: A property whose fans follow athletes can use its own brand and licensed product to build a fan relationship that isn't tied to any one player.

items.title: Disney's ESPN-led sports segment posts $4.6B in Q4 revenue, up 16%
items.summary: Disney's sports segment, which includes ESPN, reported fourth-quarter revenue of $4.6B, up 16%, with operating income of nearly $1.4B, up 53%, crediting college football and the NFL. Variety reported that growth in subscription and affiliate fees came 8% from an extra week in the quarter, 6% from higher rates and 4% from the deal giving the NFL a 10% stake in ESPN. Full-year sports revenue was $18.6B, up 5%, as Disney staff brace for job cuts.
items.what_it_means: Live sport is still lifting ESPN's results, though part of this quarter's growth came from calendar and deal effects rather than new demand.

items.title: NBA eyes infrastructure fund to help fuel Europe push, entice teams
items.summary: Citing Sky News, SBJ reports the NBA is drawing up plans for a multibillion-dollar infrastructure fund, financed by global institutions, to persuade clubs such as AC Milan, PSG, Barcelona and Real Madrid to join NBA Europe. The clubs currently play in the EuroLeague, which has rejected the NBA's efforts to acquire it. The Athletic reported the planned launch next autumn will be soft, and one source called a serious launch by October 2027 implausible.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is trying to buy its way into European basketball through arena investment, since the clubs' existing loyalties sit elsewhere.

items.title: Adobe adds U.S. SailGP Team to growing sponsorship stable
items.summary: Adobe has become the U.S. SailGP Team's Official AI Fan Experience Partner, with the team folding Adobe products into its content and marketing and using AI for faster content and insight into how fans consume it. Adobe gets branding on the catamaran and kits, hospitality and co-branded marketing. The deal follows a similar one with the BWT Alpine team last month and Adobe's existing fan experience and AI deals with the NFL, MLB, NHL and Premier League.
items.what_it_means: Tech sponsors are increasingly paying for a role in how a property makes content and reads its fans, alongside the logo.

items.title: 80% of people want AI music labeled, says Deezer/Ipsos survey
items.summary: A Deezer-commissioned Ipsos survey of 9,000 adults in eight countries found 80% want fully AI-generated music clearly labelled, and 80% say the same for AI-assisted music. US attitudes turned more negative across every general question, with the share who see AI as a valuable tool for musicians falling from 54% to 37%. Among US respondents who had heard of AI, 21% named trust as one of their feelings, down from 32% a year earlier.
items.what_it_means: Audiences are growing warier of AI-made entertainment, which raises the value of visibly human, authentic content and disclosure.

items.title: What does it mean to 'know' your fans?
items.summary: At SBJ's Fan Data Roundtable, AMB Sports and Entertainment COO Tameka Rish defined knowing a fan as having consent and a way to communicate with them, and estimated her organisation knows about 30% of its attendees on average. The biggest gap is groups where one person scans everyone in, which also skews demographic data, especially for women. The PWHL's Jayne Bussman-Wise said 40% to 80% of its attendees are first-time visitors to the arenas it plays in, and the Red Sox's Jon Hay said frictionless, genuine incentives to engage digitally during games are the clearest path to fans identifying themselves.
items.what_it_means: Most sports organisations can identify only a minority of the people in their venues, and the gap is widest among the people who come with the ticket buyer.

items.title: Leagues increasingly helping teams know, reach their fans
items.summary: The NBA launched a leaguewide data initiative four years ago that pools fan data and shares it with teams, and this season it is making sure every team has a customer data platform, providing one at its own cost if necessary. The NHL gives teams a consolidated fan view that includes league events and merchandise data, and MLB clubs such as the Red Sox now have mostly real-time access to digital data that MLB once owned outright. The PWHL, a single-entity league, runs marketing, email, analytics and ticket operations centrally.
items.what_it_means: Leagues are becoming the data infrastructure for their clubs, which shifts the advantage to whichever clubs do the most with the shared data.

items.title: Answering the ticket sales conundrum
items.summary: At SBJ's Fan Data Roundtable, the NBA's Mike James said it is easy to keep selling tickets to businesses and people with money to spend, and asked what the industry has done to nurture first and second-time buyers if the market cools. The Detroit Lions' Ashton Mullinix said the club has sold out, has a waitlist of 20,000 people and has raised prices by more than 20% a year three times in a row. Aramark's Scott McDade cited research with Vision Insights finding 80% of premium buyers want a mix of experiences, and the PWHL's Jayne Bussman-Wise said fans want different kinds of nights at different times.
items.what_it_means: A sold-out market can hide a weak pipeline of new fans, which only shows when demand turns.

items.title: NFL teams build on their investments in Mexico ahead of league's return
items.summary: Ahead of the 49ers-Vikings game in Mexico City on 22 November, NFL teams with Mexico marketing rights describe the year-round work behind it. The 49ers say their fan base there has grown by more than 1,000% since 2022 on NFL measures, have been the top-selling team on NFL Shop in Mexico for five years and plan a flag football program in 75 schools. The Rams lean on Spanish-language social, youth flag football and a children's book, while the Chiefs used Spanish-first content to climb into the top five most popular NFL teams in Mexico.
items.what_it_means: International fan bases are built through year-round local presence, with the game itself as the showcase.

items.title: Nike ends Adidas' Champions League ball reign with €40m-a-year deal
items.summary: Nike will become the official match ball supplier of the UEFA Champions League from next season until the end of 2030/31, ending Adidas' 25-year association with the competition. Nike will also supply the Europa League and Conference League, the first time one company has covered all three UEFA men's club competitions.
