SportsPro understands the deal is worth around €40 million a year, which the Financial Times reported is double the current agreement, and it followed a competitive tender run by UC3 and Relevent Football Partners.
items.what_it_means: Category rights in elite football are repricing fast, and long incumbency counts for little when a rival will pay double.

items.title: NWSL Championship Shattering Ticket Records: 'Perfect Storm'
items.summary: On Monday morning the cheapest resale ticket for Saturday's NWSL Championship between the Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current at Audi Field was $430, according to TicketData, when no previous NWSL final had passed $100. TicketData founder Keith Pagello put it down to the Spirit playing at home, brokers largely overlooking the event and heavy fan interest during the presale. Last season's final had a $64 get-in price, and prices peaked at $755 after the Spirit's semifinal win before easing.
items.what_it_means: Demand for women's sport is running ahead of how the market, resale brokers included, has been valuing it.

items.title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
items.summary: Sid Lee Sport and sister agency Kepler are evaluating Guinness's global sports sponsorship portfolio across six markets, including Great Britain, Ireland and the United States, and nine rights holders including the Premier League, Arsenal and the Six Nations. The work analyses three years of sales, brand and partnership data to isolate the incremental commercial impact of the partnerships, looking past media exposure to pouring rights, fan research and activation. Sid Lee Sport's Mike Grumbridge said traditional exposure and reach metrics don't tell brands what their investment delivers commercially.
items.what_it_means: Major sponsors are moving the test of a partnership from exposure to incremental sales.

items.title: FanSided launches redesigned app with emphasis on personalized feeds, in-depth coverage
items.summary: FanSided's redesigned app, launched on 16 November by Minute, combines personalised team feeds, analysis, video highlights and, for the first time, live scores and game tracking. The aim is to convert part of an audience of more than 50 million monthly readers into regular app users and reduce reliance on search and social referrals. Founder Zach Best said success is about retention and frequency, and that the app competes on depth of team coverage rather than trying to out-score the national apps.
items.what_it_means: Sports publishers are moving to own direct audience relationships as search and social referrals become less dependable.

items.title: TikTok says more than 46,000 UK music creators have gone LIVE in 2026, with daily views up 74% YoY
items.summary: TikTok says more than 46,000 UK music creators went LIVE on the platform between January and mid-October 2026, and that UK music creators averaged 4.9 million global views a day on TikTok LIVE in September, up 74% year on year. The company positions the feature as a way for musicians to reach listeners worldwide without the cost and logistics of touring, with income from virtual gifts on top of gigs and recorded music. It released the figures alongside a TikTok LIVE music showcase in London featuring ArrDee and Matilda Mann.
items.what_it_means: Live music audiences are increasingly being built and monetised online between tours.

items.title: Bill Simmons ends ChatGPT deal after fan backlash
items.summary: SBJ reports that Bill Simmons has ended a ChatGPT sponsorship deal after fan backlash. The sponsored segments ran mainly on The Bill Simmons Podcast and The Ringer Fantasy Football Show and worked AI-generated prompts into the discussions. SBJ cites The Wrap's view that the move shows the limits of AI companies' push into podcast advertising, where paid integrations risk alienating the audiences they are meant to reach.
items.what_it_means: Sponsor integrations built into the content itself only work if the audience accepts the fit.

items.title: Madkour: Is anything being overlooked?
items.summary: Abraham Madkour recounts a Clemson University sports marketing class where a student asked what challenges sports leaders are overlooking. His answer was whether the industry is meeting consumers' actual desire for sport in a bullish market full of new leagues, events and startups, warning against conflating investor desire with what the market wants. He also cautioned against pricing out the everyday fans who built the business, and noted the students' questions on premium experiences, private equity and global expansion.
items.what_it_means: With money pouring into new leagues and events, real fan demand is the test that matters, ahead of investor appetite.

items.title: NHL's next TV deal will test the league's strength
items.summary: The NHL can begin formal talks with ESPN and Skydance-owned TNT Sports on 1 January and is asking for a 50% to 100% increase over the seven-year, $4.5 billion deal it signed in 2021, according to sources who spoke to CNBC. The league can point to record playoff audiences averaging 1.8 million a game, a regular season up 25% and huge ratings for international hockey, while Skydance's priorities are paying down debt and funding a possible NFL increase of $1 billion a season or more. CNBC frames the outcome as the first public test of how media companies value sports rights outside the NFL.
items.what_it_means: The NHL's price will set a marker for what broadcasters and streamers pay for sport beyond the NFL, with MLB next to market.

items.title: PGA of America ready for Frisco closeup with 2027 PGA Championship
items.summary: The 2027 PGA Championship at PGA Frisco in Texas, the first men's major in the state since 1969, has sold all championship-round passes and all weeklong and daily hospitality inventory six months out. Championship director Jason Mengel said gross revenue will beat the 2026 record by 10% to 20%, and the hospitality build will pass 500,000 square feet, the largest in the event's history. The PGA of America says taking the championship to new markets that are excited to host it is part of how it grows the game.
items.what_it_means: Scarcity in a new market can sell out a major's premium inventory months before the event, freeing organisers to focus on the fan experience.

items.title: Modelo becomes NCAA's first-ever official beer in landmark partnership
items.summary: Constellation Brands' Modelo has become the first official beer of the NCAA, with exclusive beer-category rights across more than 90 men's and women's championships, including March Madness. Modelo will lift its college basketball investment by 65% year on year, run its first ad campaign built for the tournaments and activate through broadcast integrations on CBS, TBS, TNT and truTV, retail promotions and on-site experiences. Constellation's Mallika Monteiro said its sports investments start with what fans are passionate about and where they spend their time.
items.what_it_means: Newly opened alcohol categories give college sport a fresh sponsorship revenue line, and the first buyer has taken year-round access across the championship calendar.

items.title: Creator Sports Events Are Becoming Premium Branded Video
items.summary: Drawing on Tubefilter's weekly ranking of the most-watched branded YouTube videos, WeRSM notes the list is dominated by boxing, golf, football and creator-led entertainment. The Internet Invitational, a creator golf tournament whose first episode brought 64 golfers together for more than five hours, reached 12.1 million views with Reese's, DraftKings, Dunkin and ZYRTEC across the property, while DAZN and Lowe's backed other sports-led creator content. The piece argues brands are increasingly buying into creator formats that already behave like programming.
items.what_it_means: Creator-made sports events are becoming sponsorable media properties that compete with traditional sport for fan time and brand budgets.

items.title: MotoGP and ESPN Announce Two-Year Media Rights Agreement for U.S. and Latin America
items.summary: MotoGP has signed a two-year deal making ESPN its exclusive US media rights holder across linear networks for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, with races shown live or on same-day delay. In Latin America, ESPN continues coverage across 18 countries with streaming on Disney+, and rights for select events in Argentina and Brazil can be sublicensed to free-to-air broadcasters. MotoGP deputy CEO Carlos Ezpeleta framed the deal as a chance to introduce the sport to new audiences while serving existing fans.
items.what_it_means: Smaller global properties are using the reach of a major US broadcaster to find new fans in the Americas.

items.title: Yamaha Corporation to Acquire Disguise for Next Phase of Growth
items.summary: Yamaha Corporation has announced it will acquire Disguise, the visual technology company behind live experiences for tours by Beyoncé, Taylor Swift and Bad Bunny and venues including the Stade de France. Yamaha said people are seeking richer, more immersive live entertainment where audio, video, lighting and media come together across an entire space, and the deal combines its music heritage with Disguise's visual technology.
items.what_it_means: Major equipment makers are betting on immersive live production as audiences expect more from a night out.

items.title: Nascar's been building a fan database for years. Will a larger fanbase follow?
items.summary: NASCAR has run a customer data platform in some form for about a decade, but only recently started using it to move people through the fan funnel, according to VP of performance marketing Cara Verwholt. The league is working with Two Circles and a committee of stakeholders, including track owners and promoters, to agree shared definitions of a new fan and an engaged fan by December, ahead of the 2027 season. A key gap is that fans who visit tracks NASCAR does not own may never reach its data platform.
items.what_it_means: Fan data only pays off when every party touching the fan agrees what a fan is and shares what they learn.

items.title: Netflix, AEG Presents Unveil 2027 North American Dates For 'KPop Demon Hunters Golden World Tour'
items.summary: Netflix and AEG Presents announced the KPop Demon Hunters Golden World Tour, presented by Mastercard, opening in June 2027 with 25 initial shows and plans for more than 150 performances across North America, the UK, Europe, Latin America and Asia Pacific through 2028. Some markets get matinee and evening shows on the same day, and VIP packages include on-stage photos and limited memorabilia. Netflix CMO Marian Lee pointed to 63 consecutive weeks in Netflix's Global Top 10 and more than 2 billion Spotify streams for 'Golden'.
items.what_it_means: A streaming hit is being turned into a ticketed arena business, with the fandom built on screen paying off in seats, presales and merchandise.

items.title: NASCAR still searching for next mainstream talisman, catalysts for upping driver star power
items.summary: NASCAR is looking for a driver who can break into the mainstream, and Carson Hocevar's first Cup win in April drove diecast sales for him that rank as the most for any race win since NASCAR and Lionel formed their joint venture in 2010. The SRSS Sports Poll found 64% of NASCAR fans have no favourite driver, the highest in more than 25 years and more than double the 2009 figure. Cup Series viewership averaged 2.419 million in 2026, down 2%, and NASCAR is paying drivers through an ambassador bonus pool for promoting the sport off the track.
items.what_it_means: When most fans have no favourite athlete, a sport loses one of its strongest reasons for people to come back each week.

items.title: U.S. Open Revenues Continue Hot Streak, Records Show
items.summary: The US Open brought in $637.9 million in 2025, up 14% on the previous year and more than double its 2016 revenue, with implied operating profit of about $313 million. Ticket sales were the biggest driver, up 21% in 2025 and 50% since 2022, even as fan complaints about prices continued. Licensed merchandise was the fastest-growing segment, up 43% to $17.2 million, and players are pushing for a bigger share of Grand Slam revenue.
items.what_it_means: A two-week event has turned itself into a destination people pay more for each year, and the next fight is over who shares in that growth.

items.title: How Gotham FC Pulled Off a Sudden Semifinal Stadium Relocation
items.summary: After players called the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium unplayable, Gotham FC moved its NWSL semifinal to the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium on Randall's Island, which has no subway access. The club added premium seating, a fan festival and food trucks, ran free ferries and charter buses from New Jersey, and spent $8,000 on bar tabs for watch parties for fans shut out of the smaller venue. Gotham had been calling venues across the tri-state area since summer in case broadcast windows clashed with the Red Bulls' schedule.
items.what_it_means: When the venue shrinks, the club has to look after the fans who cannot get in as well as those who can.

items.title: College Notes: '27 CFP Championship in Vegas to have free fanfest, experiences at the Strip
items.summary: The 2027 College Football Playoff National Championship at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas will include a free fanfest, a free two-day concert series, a food tasting series and a running event on part of the Strip, citing the Las Vegas Review-Journal. CFP executive director Rich Clark said it is important to involve the host city because not everyone can afford a ticket or has time to attend the game.
items.what_it_means: Big events are building free experiences around the game to reach the much larger audience who will never hold a ticket.

items.title: WTA Chair Believes She Has Road Map Out of Financial Hole
items.summary: WTA chair Valerie Camillo told Front Office Sports she is reassuring players about the organisation's future after reports it was on track for a $23 million loss in 2026. The men's tour grew revenue from $144 million to $294 million between 2018 and 2024 while the WTA grew from $103 million to $143 million, and the WTA expects revenue to fall to $112 million in 2026 after the Saudi Finals deal ended. It has committed to prize money parity with the ATP despite a revenue base less than half the size, and Camillo said merger talks with the ATP have continued on and off.
items.what_it_means: Interest in women's sport is rising faster than the WTA's ability to turn it into revenue.

items.title: Fox's Mulvihill: NFL gains impressive; Bears, Rams gaining
items.summary: Fox Sports' head of insights and analytics Mike Mulvihill noted NFL average viewership is up 2% after Week 9, and said that gain is more impressive than last year's records because there is no Nielsen Big Data tailwind this season. Rams viewership in Los Angeles is up 86%, far ahead of the Raiders at 34%, while Chicago now has the most people watching their local team, with Bears ratings up 16%.
items.what_it_means: Local audiences can swing sharply with team form, which changes what a local broadcast or sponsorship is worth year to year.

items.title: Yankees report $355.7M in '26 ticket and suite license revenue through Sept. 30
items.summary: The Yankees reported $355.7 million in ticket and suite license revenue for the 2026 regular season and AL Wild Card round, up from $339.5 million over the same span last year, according to a ballpark bond disclosure. Total regular-season attendance fell from 3.393 million to 3.297 million.
items.what_it_means: Revenue per fan is rising even as fewer people come through the gates, which puts more weight on the value of each attendee.

items.title: Symphonic inks deal to bring 'hundreds of thousands' of songs to Roblox, with artists paid royalties for all plays
items.summary: Music distributor Symphonic has signed a deal with Roblox to bring hundreds of thousands of curated songs into the Roblox Creator Store, with artists paid royalties for every play. Developers can preview tracks and place them in games through sound objects and jukeboxes, and the music can also be used in Moments, Roblox's feed of shared gameplay clips.
items.what_it_means: Gaming platforms are becoming paid places for music discovery, where younger audiences find artists inside the games they already spend time in.

items.title: In Bilt deal, Texans see a highly personalized fan experience in the future
items.summary: The Houston Texans will build Bilt's white-label loyalty and rewards platform into their fan app, with a launch expected for the 2027 season. Team president Mike Tomon said the aim is to show value to season ticket holders and fans outside game day, through rewards that work across retail, restaurants and other everyday spending all year. The Texans also plan to use Bilt's neighbourhood payments product in their planned Toro District development, and see Bilt's AI fan concierge as a route to personalised rewards and richer fan data, such as a free drink at a partner bar when the Texans score.
items.what_it_means: NFL clubs are starting to treat everyday spending away from the stadium as part of the fan relationship, with rewards designed to run 365 days a year.

items.title: Skin-Crawling Pharma Ads Crowd Out Deadlier Diseases on Sports TV
items.summary: Citing iSpot data, Sportico reports that spending on ads for skin-condition drugs in US live sports broadcasts rose 42% to about $196M in the first ten months of 2026, making it the biggest pharma category in sports TV, just ahead of weight-loss drugs. GLP-1 sports TV spend is up 131% year on year, while cancer drug spend in sport fell 32%. The column argues live sport is the most reliable way to reach older Americans at scale, noting the NFL is averaging 18.3 million viewers a game against 3.43 million for non-sports primetime programming.
items.what_it_means: Live sport's mass reach keeps pulling in big-budget categories like pharma, which shapes who funds sports broadcasts and what fans sit through.

items.title: English Soccer Still Inundated by Gambling Ads Despite Jersey Ban
items.summary: The Premier League's voluntary ban on gambling sponsors on the front of shirts took full effect this season, but Front Office Sports argues it is largely cosmetic. A University of Bristol analysis of the opening weekend found the ban removed about 10% of gambling messages, with roughly half of that offset by more exposure on sleeves, training kits and pitchside LED boards. Ampere Analysis estimates the eight affected clubs lifted their front-of-shirt deal values from $89M to $99M a year, while league-wide sleeve and training-kit sponsorship grew from $176M to $206M, largely by moving gambling deals to those spots.
items.what_it_means: When one sponsorship asset is restricted, the money tends to move to other assets rather than leave, and clubs that plan for that can protect or grow revenue.

items.title: How the BBC is using AI to transform live sport, and why it's licensing the tech to rivals
items.summary: BBC Research and Development built Signals, a platform that adds live data, AI, commerce and game elements on top of a live video feed so each viewer can personalise what they see. It ran on every live BBC broadcast from Wimbledon's Centre Court this year, with player stats, record-moment animations and two-way quizzes. The BBC says viewers spent an average of just over 30 minutes with it and 75% kept it switched on when given the choice to turn it off. The BBC sees football, athletics, cricket, motorsport and entertainment as next, and plans to license the technology to other broadcasters.
items.what_it_means: Broadcasters are trying to bring second-screen interaction into the main broadcast itself, keeping viewers engaged on the feed instead of on their phones.

items.title: Lions, Patriots see Munich game as inflection point in their Germany plans
items.summary: The Detroit Lions and New England Patriots, who have been building German fan bases since 2024 and 2022, are using their game at Munich's Allianz Arena to cash in that groundwork. More than 22,000 fans registered for a two-day Lions fan fest with concerts in central Munich, sponsored by naming rights partner Ford, and the Lions say 20% of new membership growth in their global digital fan club has come from Europe. The Patriots are running city tourism activations, a local streetwear merch drop, a broadcaster watch party and sponsor hospitality.
items.what_it_means: International fan development in the NFL is a multi-year build where the game itself is the payoff moment for fan clubs, sponsors and merchandise.

items.title: Nadal's Richard Mille partnership keeps paying off after retirement
items.summary: Summarising a Financial Times report, SBJ says Rafael Nadal's partnership with watchmaker Richard Mille continues to pay off two years after his retirement. Since 2010 Nadal has worked on 11 watches bearing his name, and the brand has grown from 2,350 watches and $87M in revenue in 2010 to an estimated 6,000 watches and $2.1B in sales last year. Having Nadal wear the watches in competition, to show their durability, became the core of the brand's sports sponsorship approach.
items.what_it_means: Athlete partnerships built into the product and seen in competition can keep delivering long after the athlete stops playing.

items.title: Washington sells football stadium naming rights to Columbia Bank
items.summary: Pending Board of Regents approval, Husky Stadium will become Columbia Bank Stadium in 2027 under a 10-year, $70M deal that also makes the bank a signature partner of the University of Washington. At $7M a year it is the largest football stadium naming rights deal in college sports. With the Alaska Airlines arena deal renewed in March, the school will earn close to $100M from naming rights over the next decade, up from a combined $42M deal previously.
items.what_it_means: College stadium naming rights are now priced like pro assets, with regional brands paying a premium to be attached to big local fan bases.

items.title: White paper: Training facilities reshape women's sports sponsorships
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports on a white paper from design firm Populous and advisory firm Comeback Ventures on how companies are rethinking sponsorship of women's sports training facilities. It says sponsors are seeking immersive engagement through partnerships instead of treating exposure as static inventory. Facilities are framed as daily athlete environments, content production hubs, youth development sites and year-round destinations for fans, giving brands more touchpoints with athletes and fans.
items.what_it_means: In women's sport, training facilities are becoming year-round sponsorship assets, helping fund the capital teams need to compete.

items.title: Tour timing leads to Q3 live entertainment contraction for CTS Eventim
items.summary: CTS Eventim's revenue fell 5.3% year on year in the third quarter, driven by an 11.7% drop in its live entertainment division, which the company put down to the timing of major tours and a strong comparison quarter in 2025. Over the first nine months, group revenue rose 8.1%, ticketing revenue grew 13.1% and live entertainment adjusted profit rose 17%. Ticketing revenue grew 11.5% in the quarter to EUR 235.4M, helped by price mix and more tickets sold.
items.what_it_means: Europe's biggest ticketer is still growing, but quarterly live entertainment results swing heavily on which big tours land when.

items.title: NBA Doubles Down on Kenny Beecham, Enjoy Basketball
items.summary: The NBA has expanded its content deal with creator Kenny Beecham and his Enjoy Basketball brand, growing the Enjoy the NBA Trivia Show from a three-episode pilot to an eight-episode season across NBA TV, the NBA app and Enjoy Basketball's YouTube channel. Other Enjoy Basketball shows will also run on NBA platforms, with a live show at the NBA Crossover fan festival during All-Star weekend, and the deal lets the creators use official NBA footage.
items.what_it_means: Leagues are bringing independent creators inside their own channels to reach fans who follow the sport through personalities rather than broadcasts.

items.title: ATP reports 49% increase in partnership revenue as sponsorship portfolio expands
items.summary: The ATP says its central partnership revenue rose 49% in 2026 and passed $100M for the first time, more than three times its 2022 level. New deals with Julius Baer, EQT and K-Swiss plus bigger spending from existing sponsors drove the jump, according to Reuters. Chief business officer Daniele Sano said more than 70% of partnership revenue is paid to tournaments for the on-site rights and activation they provide.
items.what_it_means: Centrally sold tour sponsorship is growing fast, and most of the money flows to the events that deliver activation on site.

items.title: NFL Viewership Climbs As ESPN, Amazon Deliver Double-Digit Gains
items.summary: Through Week 9 the NFL is averaging 18.3 million viewers a game, its second-highest mark on record at this point of a season and up 2% on 2025. The weekday packages are doing the lifting: ESPN's Monday Night Football is averaging 19 million, up 24%, and Amazon's Thursday Night Football 17.2 million, up 13%. The league holds the top 49 shows of the current US television season.
items.what_it_means: Weekday streaming and cable windows are now growing the NFL audience faster than its traditional Sunday slots.

items.title: Premier League clubs struggle to attract buyers amid growing sell-off
items.summary: Citing Miguel Delaney of The Independent, SBJ reports that at least eight Premier League clubs, over a third of the league, are officially or unofficially for sale, but there are very few buyers. Sources describe stagnation at the top end, with only fractional or minority deals getting done where they represent real value. Most clubs no longer have growing revenues, and the English game is seen as having topped out, which could show in the next broadcast rights cycle.
items.what_it_means: Investors are cooling on Premier League clubs because revenue growth has stalled, putting pressure on clubs to find income beyond broadcast.

items.title: LOVB Houston sees record ticket sales, growing sponsorship interest ahead of third season
items.summary: LOVB Houston, one of the professional women's volleyball league's original six teams, says ticket revenue has already passed last season's total and its home opener is trending toward a sellout. Chief business officer Lisa Walker expects the team to set league records for corporate partnership revenue by year's end. The club moved home games to the Berry Center for free parking, central access and a consistent fan experience.
items.what_it_means: A third-season women's team is growing tickets and sponsorship together by making the game-day experience easier to attend.

items.title: Report: Skydance to review Europe Olympics rights amid cost-cutting efforts
items.summary: Citing Variety, SBJ reports Skydance will look closely at its financial commitments to sporting events, including the Eurosport Olympic rights across 49 European territories for 2026-32 that it inherited from Warner Bros. Discovery and shares with the EBU. Insiders say cost savings from the Paramount acquisition could approach $3B. The company also plans a big push in early 2027 to bundle HBO Max and Paramount+.
items.what_it_means: Even marquee rights are being reassessed when a media owner's priority shifts to cutting costs and building a streaming bundle.

items.title: PGA Tour sponsorship revenue rises 14% past $1B
items.summary: The PGA Tour says sponsorship revenue rose 14% this year to more than $1B, led by Rolex alongside AWS, Raymond James and AbbVie, according to Bloomberg. Chief commercial officer Dhruv Prasad said the market appears to be validating the Tour's new direction. Sponsors are signed for almost every event in its new Championship Series, with talks under way for Challenger Series tournaments.
items.what_it_means: Sponsors are backing the PGA Tour's restructured schedule, pushing its partnership revenue past $1B.

items.title: Royals to lean on Elevate for new ballpark fan experience and sales consultation
items.summary: The Kansas City Royals have hired Elevate as exclusive sales agent for premium seating and corporate sponsorship at their proposed $1.9B ballpark, which is due in 2030. Elevate will also provide strategy, research, creative and executive search. The 34,000-seat park sits within a roughly 100-acre mixed-use development with Hallmark, a $3B project in total, with Delaware North on food and beverage and Legends as owners' rep.
items.what_it_means: New ballparks are being sold as year-round mixed-use districts, with premium and sponsorship planned years before opening.

items.title: As combat sports grows in popularity, Apple adds UFC section for Apple Sports app
items.summary: Apple has added a UFC section to its Apple Sports iPhone app, starting with UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. Fans who pick UFC get the full fight card, live round-by-round scoring, fighter records and a silhouette showing where strikes land, with lock-screen widgets and Apple Watch updates. The app, launched in 2024, now comes pre-loaded on new iPhones.
items.what_it_means: Platform owners are building sport-specific second-screen features to hold fan attention during live events.

items.title: Sodexo Live a bright spot during parent company's tough 2026
items.summary: Sodexo Live's North American revenue rose 7.3% to $1.76B in 2026, helped by a nearly 13% jump in the fourth quarter, while Sodexo North America overall fell 1%. The sports and entertainment, convention and airport unit renewed the Mariners, returned to the Florida Panthers' arena and added college accounts, and benefited from seven World Cup matches at Hard Rock Stadium. Parent Sodexo's overall revenue dipped slightly.
items.what_it_means: Spending at live events kept growing in 2026 even as the wider contract-catering business softened.

items.title: Highmark Stadium family gameday costs questioned at panel
items.summary: Consumer advocates told a New York Assembly hearing that Buffalo's Highmark Stadium is the most expensive in the NFL for a family of four, at more than $2,190 a game, citing an Action Network analysis. That is more than $700 above the league average, according to the Buffalo News. The committee is examining concession prices at venues and the idea of street pricing, where food and drink cost the same inside as outside.
items.what_it_means: The total cost of a family day out is drawing political scrutiny, which raises the stakes on the value fans feel they get.

items.title: Stadium Boom Brings New Pressure to Deliver Beyond Game Day
items.summary: Speaking at Sportico's Invest New York event, Related Companies president Bruce Beal Jr. said it is a fallacy that building a stadium automatically improves everything around it. He and Pat Ryan Jr., who oversaw Northwestern's $870 million New Ryan Field, argued the new wave of venues, now measured in billions, must anchor neighbourhoods that work year-round with housing, restaurants and retail. Related is applying that thinking at Willets Point in Queens, where NYCFC's 25,000-seat Etihad Park opens in 2027 alongside 2,500 affordable apartments.
items.what_it_means: Billion-dollar venues now have to earn their return on the days without a game, not just on game day.

items.title: Q&A: Fire's Dan Moriarty talks career, marketing brand vs. team
items.summary: Chicago Fire CMO Dan Moriarty told Ad Age, in an interview summarised by SBJ, that the pandemic accelerated digital community building because teams had to keep fans and partners engaged without live events. He said game day used to be the be-all and end-all, and now the job is growing digital audiences and working out how to monetise them. Coming from Hyatt, he described sports marketing as the opposite of a planned brand launch, because one injury, bad result or trade can undo years of work.
items.what_it_means: Team marketers are shifting effort from game day to building and monetising digital audiences that hold up whatever the results.

items.title: KPMG: Sports content spending up 57% since 2021 among leading media platforms
items.summary: New KPMG data shows sports content investment across 13 leading media and platform companies, including YouTube, Comcast/NBCU, Disney, Amazon and Netflix, reached roughly $29B last year, up 57% since 2021 and about 14% of their $207B total content spend. User-generated content spend grew faster, up 75% in five years to around $46B. KPMG's Scott Purdy said the companies that build an ecosystem around their sports rights, from UGC and gaming to bundled subscriptions and retail, will get the most from the investment.
items.what_it_means: Platforms are putting a growing share of content budgets into sport, and the payoff depends on what they build around the rights.

items.title: When baseball disappears from the screen (even the small screen), fandom suffers
items.summary: In an SBJ op-ed, communications adviser Ryan Baldwin writes that his 11-year-old son came into baseball this year through YouTube, the MLB app and roster pages he checked daily. A reported MLB memo says active players' images and video would be removed from league and club sites during a lockout, as happened in 2021. Baldwin asks MLB to explain any removal on the page, keep names and statistics visible and link to both sides' bargaining proposals, so a new fan finds an explanation instead of a blank silhouette.
items.what_it_means: For new fans the official app and site are the front door to the sport, so what a league does there during a dispute shapes fandom.

items.title: Ticket Resellers StubHub, Vivid Seats Give Dismal Earnings Reports
items.summary: Vivid Seats and StubHub both missed third-quarter targets despite a strong sports calendar that included the end of the men's World Cup and the start of college football and the NFL. Vivid Seats' shares are down nearly 80% this year, leaving it worth under $17 million against almost $2 billion at its 2021 listing, while StubHub's market value has fallen to about $2.2 billion from an $8.6 billion IPO. The piece points to resale competition, debt, regulation and internal missteps, while Live Nation, which owns Ticketmaster, reported double-digit growth.
items.what_it_means: Investors are rewarding ticketing businesses tied to primary sales and punishing standalone resale marketplaces.

items.title: Inside Diljit Dosanjh's record-breaking Aura tour
items.summary: Diljit Dosanjh became the first South Asian artist to headline Wembley Stadium, selling it out within 48 hours, after 15 sold-out North American dates grossed $32m across 225,000 fans. Live Nation's Nidhish Varughese says the team used streaming data, past ticket sales and presale demand to choose markets, including ones not usually played by South Asian tours. What surprised him most was how far fans travelled, with smaller regions in the US and UK feeding into shows in Atlanta, Orlando, Birmingham, Manchester and London.
items.what_it_means: Streaming and presale data are helping promoters find audiences in markets that never looked viable, and those fans will travel.

items.title: NHL sponsor business booming as Global Series begins in Finland
items.summary: The NHL opens its Global Series in Helsinki with 75 corporate partners and a league-record 15 global sponsors, with Procter & Gamble and Michelob Ultra among the new additions. Michelob Ultra is the league's first official US beer sponsor since the Bud Light deal ended after 2021-22. Several partners did not return, including SkipTheDishes, though the league signed a broader deal with DoorDash covering national Wednesday games and playoffs on Prime Video in Canada.
items.what_it_means: The NHL's sponsor growth is coming from global deals that follow the league into international markets.

items.title: Fourteen sponsors activating across WTGL's debut season
items.summary: WTGL, the women's version of the TGL golf simulator league, launched last weekend with 14 sponsors activating at the SoFi Center in South Florida. Twelve of the 14 are existing TGL partners, including AT&T, Best Buy, Omega and SoFi. Topgolf and Go Rentals are new and will also activate around TGL when its season starts in late December.
items.what_it_means: Bundling a women's league with an established men's property gives it a full sponsor roster from day one.

items.title: What the NBA Thinks It Will Do Better Than EuroLeague
items.summary: NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum told Sportico's Invest New York event that European basketball lags other sports in revenue despite strong fan affinity, and existing teams are tired of investing without their franchise values rising. NBA Europe will enter markets EuroLeague does not serve, including the UK, with top franchise fees expected around $1 billion. Tatum pitched new arenas as an investment case, with 30 to 40 home nights of basketball and 320 other days to fill with concerts, conferences and events.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is selling Europe on arenas that earn year-round, with basketball as the anchor tenant.

items.title: Altitude+ growth accelerates with Comcast, local distribution
items.summary: Kroenke Sports & Entertainment's Altitude+ streaming service for the Avalanche and Nuggets has grown faster since Comcast and local broadcasters widened its distribution, according to a Denver Business Journal report summarised by SBJ. Annual subscriptions tripled during the season, registered users grew 63% and total views rose 186%. KSE credits features such as extra camera angles, pre- and post-game shows, live chat and a multi-game view.
items.what_it_means: Team-owned streaming grows fastest when it is widely distributed and offers fans more than the game feed.

items.title: Disney, Mark Goldbridge and more sports: What next for The Overlap's podcast empire?
items.summary: The Overlap, the football media company started by Gary Neville, generated 2.2 billion views across platforms and 38 million monthly YouTube views last year, and was bought by UK radio group Global in January. Chief executive Scott Melvin told Sportel that because live rights are too expensive for creators, the aim is to own the conversation in the more than 150 hours a week when teams are not playing. After going ten days without discussing Ruben Amorim's sacking, it launched the hour-long Overlap Daily and partnered with fan creator Mark Goldbridge, whose United Stand channel already had 2.5 million Manchester United fans.
items.what_it_means: Creator-led media is building large, monetisable audiences around sport without owning any rights, by filling the time between matches.

items.title: Gather report shows more Fortune 500s sponsoring in women's sports
items.summary: Consulting agency Gather's third annual report compares Fortune 500 sponsorship across the WNBA and NBA, NWSL and MLS, and PWHL and NHL, and finds women's sports deals still growing faster than men's, though more slowly than last year. It identified 12 companies that sponsor only in women's sports, five of them new this year, while renewal rates sit at 86% for women's sports against 92% for men's. The gap remains wide, with the NBA holding more than twice the Fortune 500 sponsors of the WNBA and the NHL more than nine times the PWHL.
items.what_it_means: Women's sport is becoming the entry point for big brands new to sport, but a lower renewal rate shows some sponsors are still testing whether it pays back.

items.title: 65% of fans travelling abroad for concerts in Asia, report finds
items.summary: A new Concert Travel Effect in Asia report from Trip.com Group and Live Nation, based on more than 1,760 survey responses plus travel and Ticketmaster data, found 65% of concertgoers surveyed had travelled to another country or region for a show. Some 84% said they were interested in packages combining show access with travel, the ideal trip length around a show is four days, and 67% said their fan community is core to the concert experience. K-pop concerts draw nearly twice as many overseas attendees as other acts.
items.what_it_means: Concerts are increasingly driving multi-day travel spend, which makes the show the start of a bigger purchase that promoters and travel partners can package.

items.title: Skydance says it'll be 'significant player' in sports, even with debt from WBD purchase
items.summary: On its first investor call since acquiring WBD, Skydance said it will remain a significant player in sports despite a large debt load, noting that CBS Sports and TNT Sports together hold more than three dozen premium sports agreements and give it a year-round sports calendar. Executive Kevin Creighton said each rights package will be judged on audience size, engagement, advertising value, whether it drives streaming acquisition, and whether it fills a calendar gap, with every right having to earn its place. Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz highlighted that advertisers can now buy across broadcast, cable and streaming through one partner.
items.what_it_means: The newly combined CBS and TNT sports portfolio will buy rights more selectively, judging each one on whether it fills the calendar and drives streaming sign-ups.

items.title: WTA expanding consumer products program, partners with Monarch Commerce
items.summary: The WTA is launching a consumer products program, starting at this week's WTA Finals at Indian Wells with a Togethxr collaboration and a Hello Kitty licensed line, and expanding in 2027 to e-commerce and a wider licensing program. Chief brand officer Sarah Swanson said fans have never been able to buy anything representing their fandom of the WTA itself, and that the products are designed to reach different fan segments. The tour has signed Monarch Commerce for a series of drops through next year, using WTA branding, cities and tennis iconography rather than tournament or athlete marks for now.
items.what_it_means: A long-established women's tour is only now creating merchandise for its own brand, opening a new revenue stream and a way to reach new fans.

items.title: Panthers eliminating about 6,500 seats in Bank of America renovations
items.summary: Citing the Charlotte Observer, SBJ reports about 6,500 upper seats in the west end zone of Bank of America Stadium will permanently disappear to make room for a social patio, cutting capacity from 75,000 to 69,900. The Panthers are handling 1,400 PSL accounts attached to those seats, offering affected fans three options, and the buyback option has proven controversial. Another 1,000 to 1,100 nearby seats will be temporarily displaced for one or two years, and those fans are yet to be contacted.
items.what_it_means: The club is trading fixed seats for social space, and managing long-standing seat licence holders through that change is proving difficult.

items.title: Maffei-backed Horse Racing League announces details for 2027 debut
items.summary: The Horse Racing League, launched by former Liberty Media chief executive Greg Maffei and Skylark's Danny Epstien, will debut in 2027 with three race days on USA Network at Gulfstream Park, Keeneland and Santa Anita Park. Ten teams of eight horses will compete for more than $10M in prize money, with Maffei hoping to sell four teams in year one, including to celebrity partners, while six stay league-owned. He said the league will follow the storytelling model he helped install at Liberty's motorsport property, telling the stories of horses, jockeys, trainers and owners.
items.what_it_means: A new team-based format is trying to give an old sport the character-led storytelling that has grown other properties' audiences.

items.title: Ligue 1 looks to 'stress test' media rights market with complete domestic package
items.summary: Ligue 1 has taken its complete package of domestic media rights for 2027 to 2032 to market, with bids due by 3 December and a secret, ambitious reserve price, after a change to French law allowed every match and team to be sold together. This season all games air on the league's own Ligue 1+ streaming service, created after it ended its DAZN deal. LFP Media chief executive Olivier Bramly said he has spoken with close to 20 potential partners and is offering either a conventional rights deal or distribution of Ligue 1+ itself through a streamer.
items.what_it_means: Having built its own streaming service, Ligue 1 is using it as the benchmark any broadcaster must beat, and offering the service itself as an alternative to a rights deal.

items.title: Baby-care brand Coterie taps Max Homa for golf campaign highlighting parental mental labor
items.summary: Citing Marketing Brew, SBJ reports baby-care brand Coterie is moving into golf with a PSA-style campaign starring PGA Tour winner Max Homa, centred on a back-cover Golf Digest ad declaring that you never see diaper ads in golf magazines. The campaign aims to raise awareness that mothers still do most of the cognitive household labour while growing the brand's reach among fathers of young children. Homa was already a Coterie user before the partnership, and the brand has further sports marketing on its 2027 radar.
items.what_it_means: A brand outside sport is using a golf audience to reach a buyer it struggles to reach elsewhere, by placing itself where it is least expected.

items.title: P!NK Announces Sphere Residency In Las Vegas
items.summary: P!NK will play a nine-date, Live Nation-promoted residency at Sphere in Las Vegas from 29 September to 30 October 2027, the first solo female pop artist to headline the venue. Vibee is the official concert and hotel package partner, offering two-night stays at The Venetian with show tickets and VIP extras such as a fan experience lounge, crowd-free shopping hours and airport transport. Las Vegas is marking the announcement by turning the SlotZilla zipline on Fremont Street into P!NKZILLA from 11 to 19 November.
items.what_it_means: The residency is being sold as a destination trip, with hotel, VIP and city activations packaged around the show itself.

items.title: Answering 3 remaining questions about NFL shift to open distribution
items.summary: SBJ reports that Ticketmaster's new deal as the NFL's secondary ticketing partner is a seven-year agreement with a fourth-year opt-out tied to how the new open-distribution setup and its technology perform. Under that setup, licensed ticketing companies will be able to sell not only club single-game tickets but also season-ticket holders' resale inventory league-wide, and season tickets make up nearly 90% of team inventory on average. Team sources see it as a win because it widens reach and gives clubs clearer data on how many tickets are resold, by which fans and where, since a ticket resold on a site such as StubHub currently shows up only as a forwarded ticket.
items.what_it_means: Opening up resale across licensed partners gives NFL clubs far better visibility of who actually ends up holding their tickets, which has been a blind spot until now.

items.title: WTA Finals control, media rights fuel WTA's growth strategy
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that WTA chair Valerie Camillo believes the tour can close its gap with the ATP, which has about twice its revenue and five times its assets, by controlling its high-profile events and media rights. Camillo called off a proposed commercial merger with the ATP, and the WTA has now taken operational control of the WTA Finals and greater control of selling its media rights. Total revenue was $143M in 2024, up from $110M in 2019, and sources say sponsorship has doubled over the past two years to nearly $80M, with revenue expected to pass $300M by 2029.
items.what_it_means: The WTA is betting that owning its biggest event and selling its own rights will grow revenue faster than partnering with the men's tour.

items.title: CFP, ESPN reach deal on 24-team field
items.summary: The College Football Playoff management committee unanimously approved expanding to 24 teams from the 2027-28 season, with ESPN as exclusive worldwide rights holder for the expanded event. SBJ's Austin Karp reports the new deal is worth $1.7B over five years, about $340M a year, on top of ESPN's existing $7.8B CFP agreement through 2031-32. ESPN.com notes the change eliminates the Power 4 conference championship games, starts the season on a Week Zero before Labor Day and ends the regular season on Thanksgiving weekend.
items.what_it_means: ESPN is paying a premium for more playoff inventory, and the conferences are giving up their own championship games to create it.

items.title: Trail Blazers' hot start fuels surge in ticket sales
items.summary: Citing the Portland Business Journal, SBJ reports the Trail Blazers rank second in the NBA for single-game ticket sales, up 76% on last year, with group sales up 32%, as they sit 6-1 atop the Western Conference. That comes despite a summer of tension with the city over funding for Moda Center renovations. The team added 50 courtside seats that season ticket holders quickly bought, and launched a $29 Sixth Man Special that includes a ticket and a $20 food and beverage voucher for select games, which its ticketing chief said owner Tom Dundon was keen on.
items.what_it_means: A winning start is lifting casual and group demand, and the club is pairing premium inventory with low-cost entry offers to capture both ends of it.

items.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival' Headlined By Travis Scott, Cardi B, & Justice
items.summary: Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival, a one-off launch event on 21 November at Mana Wynwood in Miami, two days after the game's 19 November release. Presented with PlayStation and produced by the creators of III Points, it will feature two stages of artists from the game and its soundtrack, including Travis Scott, Cardi B, Don Toliver, Metro Boomin and a Justice DJ set. Tickets are sold through a DICE presale lottery, limited to two per code.
items.what_it_means: A video game launch is being staged as a music festival, using live performance from its own soundtrack to turn a release into an in-person event.

items.title: Fanatics, American Express collaborate on new credit card
items.summary: Fanatics and American Express have launched the Fanatics American Express Card, designed after Topps trading cards, with fans able to pick a favourite player from more than 500 NBA, NFL, UFC and WWE athletes for the card design. The card earns FanCash, Fanatics' loyalty currency, on fandom purchases and everyday spending, redeemable for apparel, trading cards, collectibles, tickets and events such as Fanatics Fest. Cardmembers also get early access to select Topps drops and can enter a Championship Challenge to have their bill paid by predicting all four major US league champions.
items.what_it_means: Fanatics is extending its loyalty currency into everyday spending, so fans earn toward sports merchandise and experiences whenever they use the card.

items.title: WTGL Has 'Surreal' Debut as Newest Women's Sports League
items.summary: WTGL, the indoor team women's golf league modelled on the men's TGL, debuted on Sunday in front of a sell-out crowd at the 1,500-seat SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, with Los Angeles Golf Club beating New York Golf Club 3-1. The league has five teams of five LPGA players, an $11 million season purse and media rights deals with ESPN and Ion, with most matches in primetime on Mondays or Tuesdays. ESPN joined the broadcast 15 minutes late because a college basketball game ran long, a problem TGL has also had, and world number one Nelly Korda has not joined the league.
items.what_it_means: Women's golf is testing whether a short, made-for-TV format can win new audiences, but it still has to compete for its broadcast window.

items.title: Bengals' Madrid trip marked by strong fan turnout, success on and off field
items.summary: Citing the Cincinnati Enquirer and The Athletic, SBJ reports that the Bengals left Madrid with wins on and off the field after a five-day trip. Bengals fans outnumbered Falcons fans at the Bernabeu by a wide margin, even though it was officially an Atlanta home game. Head coach Zac Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow both praised the turnout, and the club's operations, equipment and marketing teams were credited for planning the trip months in advance.
items.what_it_means: International games are showing that a club's fan base can travel and gather abroad, even when the club is not the designated home team.

items.title: Harlem Globetrotters balance tradition and reinvention in 100th season
items.summary: Citing The New York Times, SBJ reports the Harlem Globetrotters are closing their centennial season while trying to reach new fans without losing the traditions that made them popular. President Keith Dawkins, a former Nickelodeon executive who took over in 2022, has expanded the team's digital presence, documentaries and merchandise. Recent moves include a partnership with Drake's OVO brand, new uniforms by designer Jeff Hamilton, three seasons of a reality series on NBC and Peacock, and active Instagram and TikTok accounts.
items.what_it_means: A century-old entertainment brand is relying on fashion, content and social platforms to stay relevant when its tricks are freely available on YouTube.

items.title: Charlotte Jones reflects on growing role of women in NFL ownership
items.summary: Citing the Dallas Morning News, SBJ reports Cowboys co-owner and chief branding officer Charlotte Jones saying the NFL ownership room has changed dramatically, with a next generation bringing gender diversity that was not there before. She compared the Cowboys' family ownership with the Bengals, where Mike Brown's daughter Katie negotiates contracts and oversees business operations. Data gathered by the Cowboys shows 49.8% of the team's fans are women.
items.what_it_means: Clubs with near-even gender splits in their fan base are seeing that reflected in who runs them, and that has implications for how they market.

items.title: Championship momentum meets uncertainty in MLB
items.summary: SBJ looks at how the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays plan to cash in on their World Series runs while a lockout is expected when MLB's collective bargaining agreement expires on 1 December. The piece sets out what a title usually does for the following year: Toronto drew more than 3.3 million fans in 2026 after reaching the World Series, and the Dodgers grew sponsorship revenue 14.5% year on year according to SponsorUnited. It also recalls how the 2019 champion Nationals lost that momentum when COVID cut the season to 60 games, using ticket credits to limit refunds but still laying off business staff.
items.what_it_means: A championship creates a one-season window of demand for tickets, sponsorship and premium seats, and a labour stoppage could close that window before clubs convert it.

items.title: LIV Golf's impact felt across wider golf world
items.summary: As LIV Golf winds down, SBJ argues its lasting legacy is the change it forced across golf rather than the league itself. PGA Tour average purses rose from about $9.1M in 2021-22 to around $12.5M in 2026, and title sponsorships that could be bought for at most about $15M a year before LIV now run $30M to $35M a year for the top Championship Series events. The piece also credits LIV's broadcasts with pushing innovations such as live drone shot tracing and augmented reality graphics that are now common on PGA Tour telecasts.
items.what_it_means: A rival league that failed on its own still reset the price of sponsoring the incumbent, so brands are now paying roughly double for the same title rights.

items.title: Enhanced Games owner to acquire 77% of European promoter DEAG in all-stock deal valuing it at $115M
items.summary: Enhanced Group, the NYSE-listed owner of the Enhanced Games, has agreed to buy about 77% of Berlin-based live entertainment and ticketing company DEAG in an all-stock deal valuing DEAG at roughly US$115 million. DEAG stages more than 6,000 events a year, sells tickets through myticket.de and gigantic.com, and owns festivals and UK businesses including Kilimanjaro Live and Belladrum. Enhanced, which also sells telehealth and supplements, reported a second-quarter net loss of $61.9 million on $17.7 million revenue, and its market value is smaller than the deal value.
items.what_it_means: A loss-making sports and wellness start-up is buying an established promoter with ticketing and festivals, betting that live events give it the audience and revenue base it lacks.

items.title: Forum: Horse racing's trifecta of power, tension and objection
items.summary: Writing after the Breeders' Cup at Keeneland, SBJ's Abraham Madkour says US horse racing is consumed by tension between its power brokers over the future of the Triple Crown. He notes fans mostly know two things about the sport, the Kentucky Derby and the Triple Crown, and that the Derby's roughly 20 million viewers are what the other races market off. In June Churchill Downs offered $85 million for the Preakness Stakes rights, but Maryland, uneasy that the race could move to a Churchill-owned track in Virginia, matched and kept them.
items.what_it_means: When a sport's fan interest rests on one tentpole and one series, control of those events becomes the whole commercial fight.

items.title: NWSL prepping to move playoff games over schedule conflicts
items.summary: Citing ESPN and Bloomberg, SBJ reports that Shield winner Gotham FC could have to host a potential NWSL semifinal at the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium because its usual 25,000-seat home is booked for a New York Red Bulls friendly. San Diego Wave's home venue is also unavailable that night because of a college football game, and the national TV windows on 14 and 15 November are extremely unlikely to change. The league says it has been working with clubs and broadcasters on alternative sites, and the WNBA faced a similar problem during its finals.
items.what_it_means: Women's leagues that do not control their venues can see peak moments squeezed into smaller grounds, capping the crowds and revenue those moments should deliver.

items.title: Report: SNY cancels pair of shows, has layoffs
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that SNY, the regional sports network home of the Mets, has cancelled Baseball Night in New York and Sportsnite and laid off much of its editorial staff, effective immediately. It will keep producing Mets and Jets pre and postgame shows and the Mets Hot Stove Show. An SNY spokesperson said its site is pivoting from content to a promotional platform.
items.what_it_means: Regional sports networks are cutting back to live games and team shows, leaving the daily conversation around teams to other outlets.

items.title: Arctos' Ian Charles labels PE in college sports 'worst idea'
items.summary: Citing D Magazine, SBJ reports that Arctos Partners managing partner Ian Charles called private equity involvement in college sports the worst idea he has heard in his career, saying it seeks returns of at least 15 to 17 percent rather than acting as a safety net. He spoke alongside Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark and SMU athletic director Damon Evans, who said SMU has talked with three or four private equity groups but warned against rushing in without understanding the goal.
items.what_it_means: One of sport's biggest investors is warning that outside capital in college athletics comes with return demands that may not fit schools and their communities.

items.title: SBJ On Campus: Why the next five NFL stadiums will have roofs
items.summary: SBJ reports that when Nashville's $2.1 billion Nissan Stadium opens in April it will be the first of five consecutive new NFL stadiums that are covered, with Cleveland (2029), D.C. (2030) and Kansas City and Denver (both 2031) following, and Jacksonville adding a covering in a $1.4 billion renovation. By 2031, venues with coverings or roofs are projected to outnumber open-air NFL stadiums 16-14. Team executives frame the roof as infrastructure for year-round businesses beyond game day, including live entertainment, events and content, because weather certainty helps compete for fans' discretionary time.
items.what_it_means: NFL clubs are building roofs so the stadium can sell concerts, events and content every week, not only football Sundays.

items.title: Progressive renewing NASCAR team deal with Gibbs, stepping up to 24 primaries
items.summary: Progressive is renewing and expanding its Joe Gibbs Racing sponsorship, moving to 24 primary positions on the No. 11 Toyota next season from 18 in the deal that began in 2025. SBJ says a package of that size with JGR would typically cost well into the mid seven figures a year in rights fees. Progressive became the car's anchor after FedEx exited following 2024, and has run national comedy spots with Denny Hamlin talking to a car alongside partners such as King's Hawaiian and Yahoo!.
items.what_it_means: A major consumer insurer is buying more race inventory, not less, and treating NASCAR as national brand theatre.

items.title: 2026 WTA Finals: Can US relocation deliver the 'Super Bowl of tennis' after Saudi exit?
items.summary: SportsPro reports the WTA Finals are at Indian Wells for 2026 after the tour ended its Riyadh hosting deal a year early, with a US$10 million prize pot, US$5.5 million less than last year in Saudi Arabia. The WTA is forecasting a US$23 million operating loss in 2026 and faces the end of CVC's US$150 million investment payments in 2027, while FAGE has become title partner for the next four Finals and a Hello Kitty merchandise collaboration debuts at Indian Wells. From 2027 to 2029 the Finals move to Charlotte's Spectrum Center as the WTA also relocates its headquarters there, with Tennis Channel, Sky Sports and a new TikTok storytelling partnership in the broadcast and audience mix.
items.what_it_means: Women's tennis is trading a lucrative but contested host market for US broadcast and brand depth, and accepting a near-term financial hit to do it.

items.title: Fox closes $22B Roku acquisition
items.summary: SBJ reports Fox Corp. completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku on Friday, a deal framed as creating a larger television company that combines live sports, news and local programming with Roku's connected TV platform reaching more than 100 million households. Roku founder Anthony Wood is joining Fox's board and will co-chair Fox Digital Platforms, a new division that includes Roku, Tubi, Fox One and Red Seat Ventures. Coverage notes the close came in less than five months.
items.what_it_means: A major sports rights holder just bought the living-room operating system that decides which apps fans open.

items.title: Gotham FC sells 3,000 playoff tickets in 24 hours through Mamdani promotion
items.summary: Gotham FC sold 3,000 discounted playoff tickets in 24 hours, including 1,000 in the first 10 minutes, through a promotion with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani offering New York residents $12 seats that would normally cost $30 to $50. The club previously used a similar collaboration to help sell 4,000 tickets for July's Queens Classic at Citi Field, which drew 42,175. President of Business Operations Mark Zarthar said the mayor's Instagram and X reach also lifts sales of full-price seats among people outside the discount offer, and the push aligns with Gotham's planned 2028 move to Etihad Park in Queens.
items.what_it_means: A women's club is using a high-reach public figure as a ticket distribution channel, then converting attention into both discount and full-price sales.

items.title: 2026 Sports Media Update
items.summary: Arctos, part of KKR Solutions, argues that premium live sports media rights remain a core driver of Big Four franchise value as streaming now accounts for more than 50% of U.S. video industry economics and the bidder pool for national and local rights has expanded to at least 11 scaled players. The note says streaming and AI increase undifferentiated content, making authentic live sport scarcer and more important for retaining subscribers. It frames 2026 viewership and engagement fundamentals as strong even while mass-audience ratings for many other formats keep fragmenting.
items.what_it_means: A major sports investor is telling LPs that live sport is the content AI cannot copy, so rights scarcity still supports team values.

items.title: Skiddle secures first external investment in 25 years as Soho Square Capital takes minority stake
items.summary: UK ticketing platform Skiddle has taken its first external investment in 25 years, with Soho Square Capital buying a minority stake while founders Ben Sebborn and Richard Dyer retain control. Financial terms were not disclosed. Skiddle said the capital supports a five-year plan spanning lifestyle events beyond music and nightlife, technology and marketing, plus European expansion from its existing footprint in Ireland and several leisure destinations.
items.what_it_means: A long-independent ticketing brand is raising to follow fans into lifestyle events and more of Europe, not only music nights.

items.title: Red Bull takes to the seas and the skies for EA Sports FC event
items.summary: Red Bull's Wings Cup for EA Sports FC 27 culminates on Dec. 4 with college and open-league players, and stages the Miami final with one competitor on a boat and the other in a helicopter. The event is organised with EA Sports and PlayStation and has no outside sponsors. Red Bull is also selling Wings Cup-branded cans with codes for in-game rewards.
items.what_it_means: A drinks brand is turning a football video game final into a physical spectacle and a can that sells digital rewards.

items.title: College Football's Loaded Saturday Sets Up Huge Day for ABC, ESPN
items.summary: Front Office Sports reports Saturday is the first time in nine years that seven same-day matchups each feature two top-25 College Football Playoff teams, with Disney-owned ABC and ESPN carrying five of those games. ESPN programming executives describe building the day from a noon window through Alabama-LSU into primetime Georgia-Ole Miss, while NBC expands its Notre Dame pregame show onto Peacock. The slate arrives with college football viewership down 11% across Nielsen-rated networks this season.
items.what_it_means: Networks are stacking a rare quality slate to fight a season-long ratings slide, not celebrating a healthy audience trend.

items.title: WTGL's First Season Will Pay Players $11M in Prize Money
items.summary: Front Office Sports reports the inaugural WTGL season will pay out an $11 million purse across 25 players on five teams, with individual payouts tied to team finish and participation. Men's TGL paid $21 million in each of its first two seasons, a gap that roughly mirrors men's and women's major championship purses. A league spokesperson said the WTGL purse aligns with major championships in women's golf.
items.what_it_means: The new women's indoor golf league is pricing its first season against women's majors, not against the men's TGL headline number.

items.title: Driven By Global Growth, Live Nation Posts $10.1B In Q3 Revenue
items.summary: Live Nation Entertainment reported third-quarter revenue of $10.1 billion, up 19% year on year, as 61 million fans attended its concerts. CEO Michael Rapino said ticket sales through October reached 170 million, already ahead of all of last year, with nearly 180 million fans expected for 2026. Year to date, international markets surpassed the U.S. in both concert attendance and sponsorship revenue, and international markets drove 60% of fan growth and a majority of sponsorship revenue. Concerts revenue was $8.7 billion (up 20%), Ticketmaster $870 million (up 9%) and sponsorship $506 million (up 14%).
items.what_it_means: Live music's growth is being led outside the U.S., and brands are following the same international crowds.

items.title: Can MLS Capitalize on Son-Mania?
items.summary: Front Office Sports reports that Son Heung-min's LAFC away matches have drawn crowds in Tottenham and South Korea shirts, including at Citi Field for NYCFC. D.C. United worked with the DC Spurs supporters group on a group package that put more than 900 fans into Audi Field, and a post-event survey found more than half would attend another D.C. United match. Clubs are bundling Son games with other fixtures and reaching Korean community groups to try to turn one-off visitors into partial plans and season tickets. Son himself told FOS he still sees Spurs shirts with his name at away matches across the country.
items.what_it_means: A visiting star can fill seats with someone else's fans; the commercial test is whether clubs convert that night into ongoing membership.

items.title: Texas Tech details escalating payments in Galaxy stadium naming-rights deal
items.summary: Citing the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal, SBJ reports that Texas Tech's 15-year naming-rights deal with Galaxy Digital for Galaxy Stadium starts at $4 million in 2026-27 and rises 3% a year to more than $6 million by 2040-41, for a total of about $74.4 million. Fees are paid in two equal instalments each year, and Galaxy can opt out on 30 June 2036. The deal guarantees at least six home games a year and lets Galaxy put up to $100,000 of each year's fee toward Tech athletes' NIL.
items.what_it_means: A college stadium naming deal is bundling escalating cash with a built-in NIL spend and a mid-term exit option for the sponsor.

items.title: World Triathlon partnership boosts Hyrox's Olympic ambitions
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that Hyrox's partnership with World Triathlon makes the hybrid racing format a recognised discipline inside an Olympic sport's governing body. World Triathlon's president said the deal should help national federations grow participation and reach new audiences. The partnership removes a major barrier to Olympic entry, though it is too late for Los Angeles 2028 and any push would aim at Brisbane 2032. It is still unclear whether Hybrid Racing would enter as a new sport or as a discipline under triathlon.
items.what_it_means: A participation-led fitness brand is buying Olympic pathway credibility by nesting inside an existing federation rather than waiting for a new sport slot.

items.title: VEON to Acquire Interest in Jungo TV and All Women's Sports Network (AWSN) to Accelerate Digital Entertainment Growth
items.summary: VEON announced it will take a 33.75% equity stake, with control rights, in JungoTV Holdco, the holding company of Los Angeles-based Jungo TV. Jungo TV's portfolio includes the All Women's Sports Network (AWSN), a 24/7 women's sports channel co-founded with Whoopi Goldberg, and is distributed in more than 60 countries via platforms such as Amazon Prime Video, Pluto TV, DIRECTV, Sling, Jio, SuperSport and MBC. VEON plans to expand that programming across its markets in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Ukraine, targeting growth through subscriptions, advertising, sponsorship and content licensing. Jungo TV and AWSN will stay headquartered in Los Angeles under existing management.
items.what_it_means: A global telco is buying distribution for women's sports content into markets where it already owns the customer relationship.

items.title: Nostalgic Anaheim Ducks Hometown Remix jersey sparks surge in sales
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that the Anaheim Ducks' Hometown Remix jersey, a modern nod to Mighty Ducks movie colours, sold out on Fanatics and was the only one of the 32 Remix sweaters to do so as of Wednesday night. Team SVP and CMO Merit Tully said the club sold more than 2,000 jerseys at its team store in the first 24 hours, the most in a single day since 1993, and more than 4,000 jerseys and related items over three days. The Ducks will wear the jersey in 10 games, and Tully expects another sales lift when they do.
items.what_it_means: Nostalgia tied to a team's entertainment origin story can outsell a league-wide jersey drop when the design feels like the club's own.

items.title: In TikTok first, Raiders pregame live show draws plenty of eyeballs
items.summary: SBJ reports that before their Oct. 25 home game against the Rams, the Las Vegas Raiders ran a 49-minute pregame show on TikTok Live and counted 220,000 unique views, a format TikTok says is new among NFL teams. Rather than studio Xs and Os, the club hired TikTok personality Lycette Beatty to broadcast from inside Allegiant Stadium as fans arrived, with interviews and a focus on the Vegas spectacle. Senior director of content strategy Gavin Rivera said the goal was reach on a platform with a wide, diverse audience, and that the result exceeded expectations.
items.what_it_means: A team pregame show on TikTok can out-reach traditional studio content when it sells the night out, not the playbook.

items.title: Disney continues sports content push abroad as the Rich Eisen Show is added to select EMEA markets
items.summary: SBJ reports that The Rich Eisen Show is expanding for the first time onto ESPN on Disney+ in selected Europe, Middle East and Africa markets, including the UK, Ireland, South Africa, the Netherlands and Nordic countries. The move sits inside a wider Disney push to grow ESPN on Disney+ internationally, with the service set to carry ESPN's Super Bowl stream in more than 55 international markets in February. Disney+ also recently licensed Formula E coverage into more than 100 countries and territories.
items.what_it_means: Disney is packing talk, live sport and niche series onto the same international streaming shelf rather than treating overseas ESPN as rights-only.

items.title: As '26 season concludes, O'Donnell says NASCAR has encouraging momentum
items.summary: In his first state-of-the-sport press conference as NASCAR CEO, Steve O'Donnell said attendance across 38 race weekends was up 5% overall and up 12% for kids under 12, with social impressions up 34% despite posting less. He said interest among 18-34 fans is at its highest since 2013, while TV viewership remains strong but still a focus. Stellantis plans to bring Dodge back to the Cup Series in 2027, giving NASCAR four manufacturers at the top level for the first time in well over a decade.
items.what_it_means: NASCAR is measuring success in who shows up at the track and who comes back younger, not only in the broadcast number.

items.title: Sky Sports acquires WTGL rights
items.summary: Sky Sports has secured exclusive UK rights to the WTGL, the new women's team golf league in partnership with the LPGA, for the 2026 and 2027 seasons, alongside a further two years of the men's TGL presented by SoFi. The inaugural WTGL season begins on 8 November and will use the same mic'd-up, risk-reward team formats as the men's competition, with players including Charley Hull, Lottie Woad and Jeeno Thitikul. Sky framed the deal as part of its commitment to women's sport and to bringing fans closer to major golf moments.
items.what_it_means: A UK broadcaster is pairing a new women's team golf product with its existing men's indoor league rather than treating it as a one-off special.

items.title: Bucks making games free on TV shows commitment to fan investment
items.summary: Citing the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, SBJ reports that the Milwaukee Bucks will show all 82 regular-season games free over the air this season on MY24 and statewide affiliates through Rincon Broadcasting Group, the first time in more than 30 years. Co-owner Wes Edens said the move reaches a lot more people and was the right decision for ownership and the business. Team president Josh Glessing called it a substantial economic decision but said the club expects to have more fans a year from now than it does today. Games also remain available on YouTube TV and most cable packages.
items.what_it_means: A team is trading local rights income for free reach, betting that a bigger fan base will be worth more over time than a smaller paying audience.

items.title: LIV Golf set to close down after BC Partners withdraws US$300m lifeline
items.summary: SportsPro reports that LIV Golf is set to go out of business after BC Partners withdrew a US$300 million offer of financial support, following Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ending its backing after spending as much as US$5 billion since 2021. The funding depended on LIV signing enough players, but many of its biggest names left rather than accept reduced terms. SportsPro notes that despite the money and stars like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, LIV failed to capture the public imagination or secure a significant media rights deal.
items.what_it_means: A heavily funded league with star talent could not build the audience or media value to sustain itself, a sharp lesson on what money alone can and cannot buy in sport.

items.title: Glazer: Manchester United commercial power not dependent on team success
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that Manchester United co-owner Avram Glazer told investors at Deutsche Bank's first Sports Investment Conference in London that clubs like United are not dependent on results on the pitch for commercial power. He compared United's value to the Yankees and Cowboys, which remain major global brands regardless of sporting variance. Sources suggested the remarks were aimed at presenting the club in the best light to potential investors.
items.what_it_means: An owner is pitching a global club's brand as the asset that holds value through poor seasons, which is how investors increasingly look at the biggest teams.

items.title: Sphere Earnings Exceed Expectations Again In Q3
items.summary: Sphere Entertainment posted Q3 revenue of $274.3 million, ahead of analyst consensus, and its shares rose nearly 8% by midday. The Wizard of Oz at Sphere has passed $500 million in sales and more than 4 million tickets since its August 2025 debut, and revenue at the Las Vegas venue rose $24.8 million year on year to $198.9 million. The MSG regional sports networks moved the other way, with revenue down 15% as subscribers fell 15.5%.
items.what_it_means: Inside one company, a destination live experience is growing fast while a traditional regional sports TV business shrinks.

items.title: Ligue 1 promises a "bargain" as it eyes new French TV deal from 2027
items.summary: Ligue 1 has been without a senior broadcaster since 2025 and launched its own direct-to-consumer service, Ligue 1+, which now shows all ten matches each weekend and has around a million subscribers. LFP Media chief executive Olivier Bramly told SportsPro the league is bringing its next tender forward to cover 2027 to 2032 after streamers and pay-TV platforms showed interest. Bidders can take the rights to all matches as one bundle, which would close Ligue 1+, or exclusive distribution of the service, and Bramly described the reserve price as a bargain.
items.what_it_means: A major league that went direct to fans now wants a traditional broadcast partner back for financial certainty, a reality check for leagues weighing their own streaming services.

items.title: NASCAR sprinkles $50M onto track touch-ups as fans push for fresh experience, amenities
items.summary: NASCAR has spent $50 million this year touching up some of its racetracks and has formed a new working group to study potential renovations.
